ACC101.description:
Main objectives: 
Upon completion of this course, students should: 
1. Have clear understanding of ideas, principles, and techniques of accounting 
2. Have the knowledge and tools to better understand business performance issues, and the decisions and problems faced by managers;
3. Understand the important role of accounting and finance in all organizations, in all jobs, and its link with the development of increasingly sophisticated IT systems.
Specific objectives : 
1. Recognize and organize accounting transactions
2. Classify and calculate correctly in terms of revenue, cost, profit or loss in an account
3. Be able to prepare comprehensive and accurate financial statements 
Description:
The main content is structured into twelve chapters covering Financial Accounting, Management Accounting, and Business Finance.
Topics include: business transaction, financial statement format and analysis, inventory and accounts receivable, type of assets and liabilities, costing classification, master budget and capital budgeting
A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications, which enable students to constructivist questions while maintaining their critical thinking and originality.

ACD301.description: This course introduces essential concepts and methodologies for CMOS analog integrated circuit design, geared toward electronics engineering students with backgrounds in mathematics, physics, circuit theory, electronics, and signal processing. Emphasizing the integration of analytical and simulation approaches, the course utilizes SPICE simulations to illustrate and verify theoretical concepts, providing a practical approach to accurate circuit design.Key topics include MOS transistor modeling, basic gain stages, multi-stage amplifiers, and feedback theory, all foundational to understanding and designing CMOS circuits. The course also covers two-stage operational amplifiers and biasing circuits, with stability and feedback considerations for practical applications. It concludes with a summary of the essential equations and principles, offering students a comprehensive reference for CMOS analog design.

assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Assignment 1: Market Research and Design Direction Proposal for a Packaging System(Choose a company/shop/brand in any product category)Deliverables:1. A PDF file presenting the Market Research and the Packaging System Design Direction.2. A PDF file documenting the process of AI application and evidence of personal adjustments during the project development.Requirements:The research and design direction must cover the following components: * Market Research - Brand introduction: trade name, market segment, sales channels (traditional market/supermarket/e-commerce), target distribution areas. - Products: shape, specifications/volumes, features–functions–usage, current materials, product lines/categories. Include visual illustrations. - Customer personas: minimum of 2 personas with visual representation, purchasing behavior, motivations–barriers, and packaging selection criteria. - Product market development (if applicable): domestic/export, specific requirements (transportation, display, legal compliance). - Competitors (direct/indirect): logos, key products, SWOT analysis, quick comparison on “physical shelf” and “digital shelf” (thumbnail effect in online display). * Packaging Direction (present 3 distinct directions) - Packaging levels: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary packaging applicable to each product line (SKU). - Design direction: structure/die-cut/materials; style–color palette–typography. Present design direction with moodboards, proposed color schemes, fonts, reference images/icons, and sample packaging design examples.
assessments.gradingGuide: - Have Full range of items required - Research carefully - Present aesthetically and professionally - Create packaging design orientation suitable to customers.

assessments.questionType: A (personal) job through 3 phases that demonstrate students' ability to understand and apply knowledge about designing a packaging system from research stage to design completion stage in practice.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Assignment 2: Developing the Structural System of Primary & Secondary Packaging(multiple weights/flavors), at actual scale, using real or closely simulated materials (surface graphics not yet designed). Minimum of 3 different SKUs (e.g., 250g/500g/1kg or Flavor A/B/C).Deliverables:1. A physical set of packaging prototypes at actual size, using real or closely simulated materials (without surface layout design).2. A PDF file documenting the process of AI application and evidence of personal adjustments during the project development.Requirements:- The packaging structure must include the following components: + Primary packaging: the container in direct contact with the product (box/bag/bottle), at accurate capacity and real size. + Secondary packaging: the outer layer containing the primary unit (outer box/sleeve/tray), optimized for display and stacking. + Materials: equivalent to production-grade (e.g., duplex/ivory/kraft paper, corrugated carton, PET/PP). If not available, use the closest possible simulation. + Die-cut/dieline: with clearly indicated dimensions, folds, and glue flaps.
assessments.gradingGuide: - Calculate the die, accurate structures, safety and convenience, use the right materials. - Creativity and functionality based on sustainable design

ADS301m.description: This course is designed to teach students to optimize website content for the best possible search engine ranking. Students will learn the theory behind Google search and other search engine algorithms, as well as build practical, real-world skills that can be applied to a career in digital marketing or online content development, including on-page and off-page optimization, optimizing for local and international audiences, conducting search-focused website audits, and aligning SEO with overall business strategies. Students will also learn how to create and execute search campaigns on Google Ads Search (formally AdWords). Through an introductory overview, students are guided through the official Google Ads Search training materials. Beyond Google materials, practical campaign creation and optimization best practices and exercises are provided to ensure the acquisition of practical skills and knowledge.

clos.details: Discuss key aspects of mobile application design and development, including process stages, platform differences, and user interaction models.
Conduct domain-specific research to identify real user problems and develop a research-backed proposal for a mobile application solution.
Create sketches and paper prototypes to explore and communicate early-stage design ideas and user flows.
Build interactive digital prototypes using up-to-date design tools (e.g., Figma, ProtoPie, Framer, or similar), representing realistic app behavior.
Enhance design solutions by applying UI/UX principles, mobile-specific best practices, and visual design guidelines.
Explain and apply evaluation methods in the implementation phase, including usability testing, A/B testing, and remote testing techniques.
Conduct usability testing on mobile prototypes, gather feedback, and derive actionable insights to improve the product.
Manage project tasks collaboratively throughout the full mobile app design process, including coordination with developers and team members.
Present the design process and outcome effectively through well-structured documentation, visual storytelling presentations.

ADT401.description: This course aims to provide student understanding on techniques, tools and skills to do a practical application design project. To study this course, student must have basic knowledge related to Interaction and UX Design, understanding principles and agile process applied in a mobile design project. In this course, student will perform a design project individually and have to work with programmer to transform an idea to a product. They will learn how to do from a research to design and implement an application project. They will learn about how to run a study of domain interested, how to make use-case list and draw flow diagram. They will be taught about the way to write a proposal for a project. In design phase, there are alot of things student must aware about, so they will be taught about them including rules, principles and good practices such as Realism, Fitts's Law, Animation, Speed and etc.. Testing techniques such as A/B Testing, Usability Testing will also be explained in this course. Student will be evaluated according to how his/her applied knowledge gained from this course to the course's project.

AFA201.description:
The course equips students with basic knowledges of structure, human body proportions and practice drawing as well as human drawing. This is a foundation course for speedy drawing and animated design.
Students will study the structure of the body's anatomy, then apply the gained knowledge to perform the drawing on human model. assessments.gradingGuide: Students practices drawing. Lecturer evaluates and grades the student's drawings. Scoring scale (10 points): Built up: create overall ratio of the object accurately. Ratio of every single object, part must be match with overall layout. Build up object's structure correctly without distortion. Draw bones and muscles structure correctly. (4 points); Block and planes: create accurately fragments in accordance to the structure, suitable and appropriate values. (2 points); Demonstration: demonstrate values correctly in accordance to real space of objects, hence enable virtual space upon drawings. Though such demonstration, material and shade of objects are presented. (1 point); Technique: clear outline, good dark-bright and bold-light contrast, describe properties of objects (1 point); Emphasis: emphasis object's details reasonably (1 point); Emotion: the drawing demonstrates feelings and aesthetic (0.5 - 1.0 point). AI usage guideline (optional and supportive): After completing the core hand-drawing assignment, students may optionally use AI tools in the post-production stage to support presentation of their work. This can include: Creating simple animated movements or transitions using AI animation tools (e.g., AnimateDiff, Runway, etc.); Enhancing the drawn figures with pose exploration previews to compare anatomy proportions; Supporting visual presentation (e.g., layout suggestion, color contrast preview) without altering the hand-drawn structure. Note: The original hand-drawn artwork remains the primary product for evaluation. If AI tools are applied in the post-processing phase, students must submit an additional 1-page report (in PDF) detailing the tools used, specific steps taken, and purpose of enhancement, along with the final product. This report will be reviewed for transparency and will not affect the drawing score but may contribute to a bonus if well documented and appropriately applied.
assessments.note: Submit 03 hand-drawn papers. Submit hard copy in class. Submit soft copy to Coursera and instructor's drive link

AFA201m.description: This course provides students with fundamental knowledge of human body structure and proportions, as well as skills in drawing and sketching human figures. It is a foundational course for quick sketching and animation design. The course is offered in conjunction with Coursera's "Anatomy for the Character Design Artist". Throughout the course, students will learn about the history of anatomy, study the structure of the human body in motion, and learn how to draw the proportions of the head, shoulders and arms, legs and feet, and torso. Students will then apply these skills to practice drawing humans in various poses. Finally, students will be able to create character designs that maintain harmonious and visually pleasing human anatomy proportions. In addition, students will be introduced to the use of AI tools in supporting reference generation, pose exploration, and character design ideation, helping them enhance their visual outcomes while still maintaining core anatomy principles.

AGA301c.description: Advanced Generative AI (AGA) studies how modern large language models (LLMs) and the generative-AI stack are built, adapted, evaluated, and deployed. This technology is one of the most rapidly evolving areas of machine learning, and demand is growing for professionals able to construct, fine-tune, align, and ship production-quality LLM-based systems. The course covers transformer architectures and data preparation, foundational and transformer-based language modelling, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, QLoRA), advanced alignment (RLHF, PPO, DPO), and the design of LLM-powered applications using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), LangChain, and AI agents. By the end of this specialization, students will be ready to design generative-AI applications that perform text generation, classification, translation, retrieval-augmented question answering, and build LLM-powered agents.

clos.details:
Understand the Principles of AI/ML/DL
Grasp the core concepts, the distinctions between Supervised and Unsupervised Learning, fundamental Neural Network architectures, and the standard workflow for building a foundational machine learning model.

Understand the Cybersecurity Context
Comprehend how AI is integrated into security architectures and identify specific cybersecurity challenges that are suitable for AI-driven solutions.

Apply Basic Probability and Statistics
Apply fundamental concepts of probability and statistics to model and analyze cybersecurity data, including estimating the likelihood of attack events and evaluating the reliability and statistical significance of detection results.

Apply Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Feature Engineering
Utilize programming tools (Python/Pandas) to collect, explore, and visualize cybersecurity data (such as system logs and network traffic). Execute data preprocessing and feature engineering techniques—including data cleaning, encoding, and feature extraction—to adequately prepare input data for machine learning models.

Apply Supervised and Unsupervised Learning
Implement supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms to develop models for intrusion detection, malware classification, and anomaly detection.

Apply Deep Learning and NLP for Security
Leverage Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyze and detect deceptive content, such as phishing and spam, within text and URLs.

Performance Analysis

Analyze experimental results using a Confusion Matrix and key performance metrics (Precision, Recall, and F1-score), evaluating the operational impact of False Positives and False Negatives in real-world security environments.

Apply Imbalanced Data Handling

Employ data preprocessing techniques, such as resampling and class weighting, to resolve challenges associated with imbalanced datasets.

Analyze AI Risks and Apply LLMs in Cybersecurity

Analyze model vulnerabilities, specifically adversarial attacks, and evaluate emerging threats introduced by Generative AI, such as deepfakes and automated social engineering. Furthermore, apply Large Language Models (LLMs) and agentic AI frameworks to address and resolve complex cybersecurity challenges.

Apply Project Development
Synthesize acquired knowledge and utilize collaborative teamwork skills to design, implement, and present an end-to-end AI pipeline addressing a real-world cybersecurity problem.

AIC211.description:
This course provides foundational knowledge of machine learning (ML) and AI techniques for solving cybersecurity problems. The content focuses on modeling security challenges as machine learning problems, processing and representing cybersecurity data (system logs, network traffic, security events, endpoint telemetry), and building and evaluating models. This ultimately supports the tracking, monitoring, detection, and prevention of cyber threats to protect data and systems.

The module combines theoretical foundations (basic concepts of supervised/unsupervised learning, classification, regression, anomaly detection, model evaluation, overfitting, and ML pipelines) with hands-on Python labs using popular libraries in the cybersecurity domain (such as scikit-learn and introductory deep learning modules). Students will work with real-world cybersecurity datasets applied to tasks such as Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), malware classification, phishing URL/email detection, and user/system behavior anomaly detection.
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. Understand and explain the fundamental concepts of machine learning and how to map them to cybersecurity problems.

2. Design and deploy simple, end-to-end machine learning pipelines: data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction/engineering, training, evaluation, and model improvement for cybersecurity tasks.

3. Apply machine learning techniques to predict attack behaviors, detect vulnerabilities/anomalous activities, and support decision-making in secure system operations.

4. Build a solid foundation for advanced courses in malware analysis, threat hunting, SOC engineering, and AI system security, while gaining practical experience in developing machine learning solutions for digital security.

clos.details: Explain, at user level, how generative AI and large language models produce their output, and assess their capabilities, limitations and risks in a corporate finance context in order to identify and prioritise the use cases worth pursuing in a finance function.

Apply GenAI tools to financial data analysis and predictive analytics: preparing and structuring financial and non-financial data, performing trend, ratio, common-size and variance analysis, decomposing a result into its drivers, and building and evaluating a predictive model on financial or market data.

Apply GenAI to portfolio management decisions: drafting an Investment Policy Statement, building a strategic asset allocation that matches a client's risk-return objectives, testing diversification against real correlation data, and defining monitoring and rebalancing rules.

Design GenAI-assisted management reporting: mapping a trial balance to a reporting chart of accounts, producing summary P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, and generating variance and MD&A commentary, supported by a reconciliation and control checklist for the monthly close.

Build GenAI-assisted liquidity and planning tools: a short-term cash flow forecast with a liquidity dashboard and stress scenarios, and a driver-based 12-month rolling forecast with Base/Best/Worst scenarios and what-if analysis, communicated in an executive planning memo.

Evaluate GenAI output critically and apply Responsible AI principles in a finance department: verification against source data, confidentiality of financial and personal information, bias, model failure modes, client suitability, and disclosure of what was AI-generated.

Develop and present, in a team, an AI-powered finance deliverable that connects data, analysis, reporting, liquidity and forecast into a KPI dashboard and an executive memo, and defend its assumptions and recommendations to decision makers.

AIF091.description:
1. Course Objectives:
This short course prepares finance students and business administration students with an interest in finance to use generative AI across the work of a corporate finance function: analysing financial data, managing a portfolio, producing management reports, building predictive models, planning liquidity, and forecasting. Learners study what a large language model can and cannot do with financial information, learn the prompt patterns that make its output reliable enough to use, and practise on realistic datasets in the tools a finance department already owns. By the end of the course learners can select the finance tasks worth automating, produce an AI-assisted analysis, asset allocation, report pack, predictive model, cash flow plan and rolling forecast, verify every figure against the source data, and apply Responsible AI rules to confidential financial information.
2. Course Content:
The course covers seven of the eleven courses of the Coursera AI-Powered Finance specialisation, taken online in the published order of the module plan. (1) Introduction to Generative AI in Finance (4h): how an LLM behaves, its limits, prompt engineering for finance, screening use cases, and Responsible AI in a finance function. (2) GenAI for Financial Data Analysis (4h): preparing financial data for AI, prompting for trend, ratio and variance analysis, AI-assisted spreadsheet work, and verifying output against source figures. (3) GenAI for Portfolio Managers (4h): investment policy statements, strategic asset allocation, low-correlation assets and diversification, portfolio monitoring and rebalancing, and client-centric ethics. (4) GenAI for Automated Financial Reporting (3h): chart-of-accounts mapping, summary P&L / BS / CF, variance commentary and MD&A narrative, and a reconciliation and control checklist. (5) GenAI for Financial Analysts (3h): predictive models on financial data, market-trend forecasting, risk assessment, and the failure modes of a model. (6) GenAI for Cash Flow Managers (6h): receivables, payables and inventory, AR/AP automation with low-code tools, cash flow forecasting, liquidity dashboards and scenario-based cash planning. (7) GenAI for Financial Forecasting and Planning (4h): driver-based models, a 12-month rolling forecast, Base/Best/Worst scenarios and what-if analysis, a KPI dashboard and a planning memo.
3. Activities and Teaching Methodology:
Learners take the seven Coursera courses online at their own pace, within the deadlines set in the Course Implementation Plan, and produce one deliverable per module on the university's own datasets rather than on the Coursera exercises alone. Two live tutorial slots of 2h15' anchor the course: the first, after Module 4, reviews the deliverables submitted so far, fixes tool problems, works the analysis and reporting exercises that learners found hardest, and forms the capstone teams; the second, after Module 7, is a capstone workshop followed by the team presentations and the course close. Verification is treated as part of the work, not as an afterthought: no AI-generated figure or narrative is accepted in a deliverable until it has been reconciled to source data. All datasets used are anonymised or public; no confidential company data is entered into public GenAI tools.

AIF091.note: Specialised elective short course for Finance students from semester 7 onwards. Delivery is online self-paced on Coursera plus two live tutorial slots in class; the language of the live slots is Vietnamese, all Coursera material is in English. The Coursera specialisation contains eleven courses; APF201 uses seven of them (courses 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 11 of the provider's sequence) and the online hours in this syllabus are the durations published by the provider, not estimates. Courses 2, 3, 9 and 10 of the specialisation (Mastering Portfolio Analysis; Financial Reporting: Ledgers, Taxes, Auditing; GenAI with QUILL; Oracle EPM) are out of scope and are not assessed. This specialization is designed for those with little or no background in AI, whether you have technology background or not, and does not require any programming skills. It is designed to give you a firm understanding of what is AI, its applications and use cases across various industries. Students will become acquainted with terms like Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Neural Networks. 

Furthermore, it will familiarize you with IBM Watson AI services that enable any business to quickly and easily employ pre-built AI smarts to their products and solutions. Students will also learn about creating intelligent virtual assistants and how they can be leveraged in different scenarios.

 By the end of this specialization, learners will have had hands-on interactions with several AI environments and applications, and have built and deployed an AI enabled chatbot on a website – without any coding. 

Learners will perform several no-code hands-on exercises in each of the three courses. At the end of the last course, learners would have developed, tested, and deployed a Watson AI powered customer service chatbot on a website to delight their clients.

AIL302.description:
Machine learning is the science of getting computers to act without being explicitly programmed. In the past decade, machine learning has given us self-driving cars, practical speech recognition, effective web search, and a vastly improved understanding of the human genome. Machine learning is so pervasive today that you probably use it dozens of times a day without knowing it. Many researchers also think it is the best way to make progress towards human-level AI.

This course provides a broad introduction to machine learning, datamining, and statistical pattern recognition. Topics include: (i) Supervised learning (parametric/non-parametric algorithms, support vector machines, kernels, neural networks). (ii) Unsupervised learning (clustering, dimensionality reduction, recommender systems, deep learning). (iii) Best practices in machine learning (bias/variance theory; innovation process in machine learning and AI). The course will also draw from numerous case studies and applications, so that you'll also learn how to apply learning algorithms to building smart robots (perception, control), text understanding (web search, anti-spam), computer vision, medical informatics, audio, database mining, and other areas.

This course will be implemented through online mode. Students will learn officially the online course "Machine Learning" on Coursera. During the online learning process, students will be guided by teachers-tutors through some offline sessions on the campus, and through emails

AIP491.description:
The AI Capstone Project course is an integrative experience that consolidates the knowledge and skills acquired from the undergraduate AI curriculum into a practical, real-world application. The design of this course challenges students to apply their analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills to solve complex problems using AI technologies.

Throughout this course, students will engage with all facets of the AI project development lifecycle, including problem identification, data collection and preprocessing, model design and implementation, evaluation, and deployment. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the professional standards and expectations required to successfully execute a project of this nature.

This course is structured to be completed by small groups of 3-4 students, fostering collaboration and teamwork. Each group will be assigned a supervisor, who will offer critical support and guidance throughout the research and development process. The supervisor will assist students in refining their project ideas, conducting thorough research, developing and implementing AI solutions, composing a report on their capstone project, and preparing for the final presentation in front of the examination board.

By the end of the course, students will have not only deepened their understanding of AI principles and techniques but also demonstrated their ability to apply these concepts effectively in a team-based project. This capstone project not only serves as a significant portfolio piece but also prepares students for professional careers in the field of artificial intelligence.
AIP491.studentTasks:
(1) Select a project within the chosen AI concentration: Teams should choose a project that aligns with their interests and the scope of the AI concentration. This may involve identifying a real-world problem that can be addressed with AI solutions.
(2) Divide and schedule work: Once the project is chosen, teams should allocate tasks among members based on each individual's strengths and skills. A detailed schedule should be created, outlining milestones and deadlines to ensure timely progress.
(3) Attend all scheduled meetings with supervisor: Teams must commit to regular meetings with their assigned supervisor. These sessions are crucial for receiving guidance, discussing progress, resolving any issues, and making necessary adjustments to the project plan.
(4) Produce document and product according to project requirements: Teams are expected to produce comprehensive documentation and develop the AI product according to the specified requirements. This includes but is not limited to, designing algorithms, coding, testing, and validating the AI model(s). Documentation should detail the problem, methodology, implementation, results, and conclusions.
(5) Present and defend individual contributions in front of the examination board: Each team member must be prepared to present and individually defend their specific contributions to the project in front of the examination board. This includes explaining the rationale behind their approach, the challenges faced, and the solutions implemented.
(6) Students are required to attend at least 80% of scheduled meetings with their supervisor(s) to be eligible for the thesis or capstone defense.

It trains final-year IT students across Software Engineering, Information Assurance and Information System to build, secure and ship real AI applications AND to use AI as a partner in the software-engineering workflow. Students progress through seven connected courses — a prompt-engineering foundation, Generative AI for Business Analysis (IS), RAG application development (SE), Agentic AI with LangGraph (SE), LLM Security & OWASP (IA), and Team Software Engineering with AI (SE) — sharing a common stack and a single application thread (IS defines → SE builds → IA secures → engineer with AI), then integrate everything in an end-to-end multimodal RAG + multi-agent Capstone Project. The course is competency/completion-based: no exams, fully hands-on.
AIT091.studentTasks: Complete and earn the certificate of ALL 7 required Coursera courses, including the interspersed Guided Projects, and complete/submit the RAG & Agentic AI Capstone Project. A student passes upon completing all 7 certificates and the Capstone Project. Students are also ENCOURAGED (not required) to complete the rest of the DeepLearning.AI 'Generative AI for Software Development' specialization.
AIT091.tools: Python, LangChain/LangGraph, vector databases (ChromaDB/FAISS), Model Context Protocol (MCP), Gradio, embeddings & RAG, OWASP LLM Top 10 / red-teaming, LLM-assisted coding / pair-programming, LLM APIs.
AIT091.note: 1. Pass/Complete only. 2. Completion criteria = all 7 required course certificates (1–7) + Capstone Project (7) completed. 3. Graded quizzes inside the MOOCs. 4. The Capstone Project is auto-graded by IBM's AI system. 5. Optional bonus for completing all certificates before the deadline. 6. Encouraged (not required): complete Courses 1 & 3 of the DeepLearning.AI 'Generative AI for Software Development' specialization (Course 2 of that spec IS the required Course 6).

AIT301.description:
The developing of cloud computing, big data, open source software, and improved algorithms kicked Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the mainstream of focus in technologies nowadays. AI technologies are fundamentally changing the ways we work, live, and manage businesses. This course is designed to present to student the coherent body of ideas and methods which were contributed to the development of Artificial Intelligence discipline. Student will be acquaint with the basic programs in the field and their underlying theory and will explore this through problem-solving paradigms, logic and theorem proving, language and image understanding, search and control methods and learning. This course aims to create following results on students:

1. Graduates will have ability to work with Tensor Flow machine learning library as a framework in developing AI their applications
 MO-1a: An ability to build models by plugging together building blocks with the user-friendly Keras sequential API.
 MO-1b: An ability to build models then write the forward and backward pass, create custom layers, activations, and training loops by using a define-by-run interface for customization and advanced research from Keras functional and subclassing APIs.
2. Graduates will have a broad understanding of the fundamental theories, concepts, and applications of Artificial Intelligence.
 MO-2a: An ability to apply knowledge of Artificial Intelligence appropriate to the discipline.
 MO-2b: An ability to analyze a problem and identify and define the AI requirements appropriate to its solution.
 MO-2c: An ability to design, implement, and evaluate an AI system to meet desired needs.
3. Graduates will be prepared for careers in Artificial Intelligence field.
 MO-3a: An ability to use current methodologies, techniques, skills, and tools necessary for AI practice. 
4. Graduates will communicate effectively, both orally and in writing of Artificial Intelligence-related works.
 MO-4a: An ability to communicate effectively in AI-related works.
 MO-4b: An ability to discuss about how to control and to manage APIs of Tensor Flow library effectively.

clos.details: Understand the core concepts of Python programming, advanced data structures, and their specific applications within MLOps workflows.
Apply clean coding practices, modern testing frameworks, and efficient data manipulation using Pandas and NumPy for machine learning data readiness.
Understand the fundamental principles of MLOps, DevOps, and DataOps methodologies, including their importance in the software development lifecycle.
Design and compose software solutions using microservices architectures and automated operations pipelines to support scalable machine learning applications.
Understand the principles of ethical AI and the application of high-performance languages like Rust for zero-shot classification and efficient processing.
Understand cloud-based data engineering architectures, including data ingestion, repository creation, and secure data transformation solutions.
Apply cloud technologies (such as AWS Step Functions, AWS Lambda, and Amazon SageMaker) to build, monitor, and automate end-to-end data engineering and modeling pipelines.
Understand the fundamentals of MLflow, including the Tracking UI, model registries, and artifact management via APIs.
Apply MLflow and Hugging Face modules to package reproducible machine learning projects and deploy pre-trained models efficiently.
Implement an end-to-end Advanced MLOps project that includes infrastructure setup, automated data pipelines, model tracking, cloud deployment, and reporting.

AMO301m.description: This course provides students with practical knowledge and skills to bridge the gap between machine learning model development and production deployment. Students will master essential Python programming for MLOps, explore the integration of DevOps practices, and build efficient microservices, including the application of high-performance languages like Rust for zero-shot classification. The curriculum covers cloud-based data engineering pipelines using AWS technologies (such as AWS Step Functions, Lambda, and SageMaker) alongside industry-standard tools like MLflow and Hugging Face for model tracking, reproducibility, and deployment. Through hands-on projects, students will gain comprehensive experience in designing, building, and managing end-to-end operational pipelines for real-world AI and ML solutions.
AMO301m.studentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, and labs assigned by the instructor in class or at home, and submitting them on time.
- Laptops are to be used in class strictly for learning purposes.
- Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
AMO301m.tools: Python, AWS (SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions), MLflow, Hugging Face, Rust, GitHub.
AMO301m.note:
- The mandatory capstone project focuses on designing, implementing, and deploying an end-to-end MLOps system for a real-world machine learning application. Students progressively develop the project through four milestone reports covering infrastructure design, cloud-based data engineering, model lifecycle management, deployment, and final system integration.
- The final mark is calculated by summing the weighted scores of: Progress Test (10%), Report 1 - Infrastructure & Pipeline Proposal (10%), Report 2 - Data Engineering & AWS Integration (10%), Report 3 - Model Tracking & Deployment (30%), Report 4 - Final System Report & Group Presentation (10%), and Final Exam - Computer-based Multiple-choice Examination (30%).
- The Progress Test is conducted immediately after the completion of Chapters 1, 2, and 3 to evaluate students' understanding of Python programming, software engineering practices, MLOps methodology, cloud infrastructure, and AWS-based machine learning services.
- Reports 1 to 4 are conducted as in-class group presentations with instructor evaluation and immediate feedback. Each report represents a major milestone of the capstone project and assesses students' practical implementation, documentation quality, system architecture, technical presentation, and teamwork.
- The Final Exam is an individual computer-based multiple-choice examination administered by the examination board. The examination comprehensively evaluates theoretical knowledge and practical concepts from all course chapters, including Python foundations, MLOps methodology, cloud platforms, MLflow, Hugging Face, and production deployment. At least 70% of examination questions must differ from those used in previous semesters.
Completion Criteria: every assessment component > 0 AND Final Exam Score >= 4 AND Final Result >= 5.

assessments.questionType: Students will start from a brief provided by the instructor or propose their own 2D game idea for approval. Develop an original 2D game concept covering storyline and hook, worldbuilding, gameplay structure and core mechanics, game flow, UI flow, character system, environments, props, and item system.AI tools may be applied responsibly for ideation and consistency checks, with prompts, outputs, and refinements documented. The final submission is a detailed Game Design Document (GDD) that clearly defines and describes the planned game, presented in a professional format with full citations of sources and AI use.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Understand and apply the process of developing a comprehensive 2D Game Design Document.Demonstrate the ability to integrate storyline, worldbuilding, gameplay mechanics, game flow, UI flow, and asset systems into a cohesive concept.Practice creativity and originality in concept development.
assessments.gradingGuide: Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 2 weeks. Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly.During review sessions, students must present how AI was used, discuss AI-generated issues with the instructor, and justify their design choices before the final presentation.Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.
assessments.note: Based on the studied LO, lecturer will instruct students how to ideal, research & develop their specific game project

assessments.questionType: Based on the approved Game Design Document, create a complete 2D asset package ready for development. The package must include characters, animations, environments, props, items, UI elements, and visual effects, each with a research board, references, and design rationale. All assets must align with the narrative and worldbuilding, support gameplay actions, and maintain aesthetic strength, distinct style, and visual coherence, with brief explorations and a justified final selection.The final submission is a bundled asset package containing all required visual components presented in a structured format, ready for integration into the game engine.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Apply principles of visual design and consistency to produce cohesive 2D game assets, maintain alignment with narrative, worldbuilding, and gameplay mechanics.Present a professional game art package prepared for implementation in the development phase.
assessments.gradingGuide: Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 2 weeks. Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly.During review sessions, students must present how AI was used, discuss AI-generated issues with the instructor, and justify their design choices before the final presentation.Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.
assessments.note: Based on the studied LO, lecturer will instruct students how to develop the conceptual art for the game project.

ANO301.description: Description:- This course will arm students with the conceptual and technical knowledge needed to develop 2D game projects. There are a series of foundations for experimentation and exploration of video game design, story, character development, and winning gameplay before programming begins. The courses emphasize the self-reliance and personal expression of the gaming artist, and encourage you to take conceptual risks and develop new modes of expression and form through gaming. There will be also a series of tutorials to develop gameplay without coding. Objective: - Understand primary concepts of gaming, and an exploration of how these basic concepts affect the way gamers interact with our games.- Understand what defines a “game” and the mechanics and rules behind different types of games.- Examine how storytelling acts as a vital mechanism for driving video gameplay forward.- Understand game story flows and the strategic elements of gameplay.- Investigate key components of environment and level design.- Create successful character designs that can be applied to video games- Complete a 2d game project.Teaching method:Under lecturer’s instruction, through a series of instruction sessions, tutorials, work analysis and group exercises, students will be equipped with knowledge and skills to complete a game project.

assessments.category: Practice 1 (individual work): Script for Short Film (3-5 mins)
assessments.questionType: Write a 3–5 minute short film script that demonstrates idea development, structure, and character building, while practicing storytelling and responsible use of AI for ideation and refinement.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: • Knowledge: Principles of short film scriptwriting, including idea development, narrative structure, and character creation.• Skills: Applying storytelling techniques to write a complete short film script (3–5 minutes), developing coherent plots and characters, and using AI responsibly for ideation and refinement.
assessments.gradingGuide: 1. Presentation_Script Analysis of a Short Animated Film: Choose a short animated film and present an analysis explaining the script’s role, the development of its idea and theme, and its three-act structure.2. From Logline to Character Development: Expand a selected logline into a premise/synopsis and a compact character bible. Define goals, conflicts, and clear character arcs that align with the theme and genre. (AI may support ideation/refinement; document usage.)3. Script Structure (3-Act Summary): Write a clear outline of the story in three acts (setup, confrontation, resolution. Specify turning points, stakes, and causal links.4. Complete Scriptwriting: Write a full 3–5 page screenplay in industry format, revising from feedback and staying consistent with the outline. Submit the final draft with a brief revision log and AI process evidence.
assessments.note: Submission Files:1. Presentation slides for the animated film analysis (PPT/PDF)2. Word file containing all development steps (loglines, idea development answers, 3-act structure summary, and character profiles) (.docx)3. Final short film script (Word file, 3–5 A4 pages, correct screenplay format with proper margins, font, size, capitalization rules, and appropriate screenplay writing style) (.docx)4. AI Usage Report: Screenshots or notes showing AI-generated references/plot suggestions, with a short explanation of how they supported refinement (.docx/PDF)In-Class Work: 1. Presentation of the script analysis of a chosen short animated film. 2. Peer and instructor feedback on loglines, 3-act structures, and character designs. 3. Drafting and revising script sections during In-class sessions.

assessments.questionType: Create a 30–45 second TVC script that demonstrates clear structure, effective character design, and a strong brand message. Apply storytelling principles with professionalism, and use AI tools for ideation, storyboarding, demo video creation, or refinement while ensuring originality.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: • Knowledge: Understand 30–45s TVC storytelling and structure, character/arc essentials, and industry-standard script/storyboard conventions and timing.• Skills: Turn a brief into a logline/beat sheet and produce an industry-standard TVC script/storyboard with clear structure and characters; use AI for ideation, storyboarding, demo, or refinement while documenting usage and maintaining originality.
assessments.gradingGuide: 1. Presentation: Brand ResearchConduct a brand research study that analyzes the brand’s history, values, USP, target audience, competitors, and positioning. Use AI tools at the enhanced level to support information synthesis, data analysis, and creative exploration (e.g., generating moodboards, slogans, or initial ideas).2. TVC Scriptwriting - TVC Storyboard - Demo video for the TVCUsing insights from your Brand Research, create a 30–45s TVC with:• Script in industry format (scene headings, action, dialogue/VO, transitions).• Storyboard (≈8–12 frames) with captions and timings.• Demo/animatic video (30–45s, MP4) showing pacing and key beats.AI use: Use AI for ideation, rewrites, shot listing/storyboarding, and demo assembly. Document all AI usage (tools, prompts, sources, edits) and ensure originality and authorship.
assessments.note: Submission Files: 1. Brand Research Report: Brand analysis, audience research, competitor analysis, narrative outline, AI usage report (enhanced level) (.docx/PDF)2. Final TVC Script (docx/PDF)3. AI-generated storyboard and AI Usage Report (.docx/PDF)4. AI-Generated Demo Video and AI Usage Report: MP4 file (.mp4), resolution min. 720p.In-Class Work: 1. Presentation of the script analysis of a chosen short animated film. 2. Instructor feedback on brand research, TVC structure, and AI usage 3. Drafting and revising script sections during In-class sessions.

clos.details: Trình bày và giải thích được những nguyên lý cơ bản của pháp luật hành chính và tố tụng hành chính Việt Nam trong mối tương quan so sánh với các hệ thống pháp luật hành chính tiêu biểu trên thế giới như: dân luật (Civil law), thông luật (Common law); khung khổ pháp lý, chuẩn mực quản trị công khu vực ASEAN và thế giới, qua đó nhận diện được xu hướng hội nhập và cải cách hành chính trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hóa

Vận dụng được các quy định của pháp luật hành chính và tố tụng hành chính Việt Nam để xác định và phân tích vấn đề, đưa ra lập luận và giải pháp phù hợp cho các tình huống pháp lý phát sinh trong hoạt động quản lý hành chính nhà nước

Ứng dụng được AI trong tìm kiếm, xử lý và đánh giá dữ liệu phục vụ cho việc đề xuất các giải pháp cải cách, đổi mới thể chế, chính sách, pháp luật hành chính hoặc giải quyết các tình huống pháp lý phát sinh trong hoạt động quản lý hành chính nhà nước
Thể hiện được kỹ năng tư vấn, giao tiếp và phản biện pháp lý trong các vấn đề quản lý hành chính nhà nước và thực thi pháp luật hành chính

Thể hiện được tinh thần thượng tôn pháp luật, đạo đức nghề nghiệp và trách nhiệm xã hội trong việc thực hiện pháp luật hành chính; đồng thời chủ động học tập, tự định hướng và hợp tác hiệu quả để nâng cao năng lực chuyên môn, thích ứng với yêu cầu hành nghề pháp lý trong bối cảnh chuyển đổi số và hội nhập quốc tế.

APL201.description: Học phần “Luật Hành chính và Luật Tố tụng hành chính” trang bị cho người học hệ thống kiến thức lý luận và thực tiễn về hoạt động quản lý hành chính nhà nước ở Việt Nam, khung khổ thể chế – pháp lý điều chỉnh các quan hệ phát sinh giữa cơ quan nhà nước, tổ chức và cá nhân trong quá trình thực thi quyền hành pháp. Trên nền tảng luật hành chính Việt Nam, học phần được giảng dạy theo tư duy so sánh và hội nhập, giúp người học tiếp cận, nhận diện và phân tích xu thế phát triển của pháp luật hành chính theo các nguyên tắc quản trị công hiện đại trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hóa. Qua đó, học phần góp phần hình thành năng lực vận dụng pháp luật hành chính và tố tụng hành chính trong việc bảo đảm tuân thủ và giải quyết các vấn đề pháp lý phát sinh từ hoạt động quản lý hành chính nhà nước, đồng thời hỗ trợ người học phát triển kỹ năng tư vấn, phản biện và bảo vệ quyền, lợi ích hợp pháp của tổ chức, cá nhân trong môi trường pháp lý Việt Nam và quốc tế.The course “Administrative Law and Administrative Procedure Law” provides students with theoretical and practical knowledge of state administrative management in Vietnam and the institutional and legal framework governing relationships among state authorities, organizations, and individuals in the exercise of executive power. Grounded in Vietnamese administrative law, the course is taught through a comparative and integrative approach, enabling learners to explore, identify, and analyze current trends in administrative law in light of modern principles of public governance within a globalized context. The course thereby fosters the ability to apply administrative law and administrative procedural law in ensuring compliance and addressing legal issues arising from public administration activities. It also equips students with the skills to provide legal advice, engage in critical analysis, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of organizations and individuals within the legal frameworks of Vietnam and the international context.

This includes the ability to design and implement classes, utilize inheritance and polymorphism, and understand the benefits of encapsulation. Students will gain practical experience in building graphical user interfaces (GUIs) for their applications, enhancing user interaction and visualization. Furthermore, they will delve into the world of concurrent programming, learning how to write multi-process programs that leverage the power of modern processors for increased speed and efficiency. Students will explore the fundamentals of network systems and acquire the skills to develop networked applications, including client-server programs, using socket programming in Python.

ASR301c.description: This course is about using AI in scientific situations to discover trends and patterns within datasets. Course 1 teaches a little about the Python language related to data science. We'll share some existing libraries to help analyze your datasets. By the end of the course, you'll apply a classification model to predict the presence or absence of heart disease from a patient's health data. Course 2 covers the complete machine learning pipeline, from reading in, cleaning, and transforming data to running basic and advanced machine learning algorithms. In the final project, we'll apply our skills to compare different machine learning models in Python. In Course 3, we will build on our knowledge of basic models and explore more advanced AI techniques. We’ll describe the differences between the two techniques and explore how they differ. Then, we’ll complete a project predicting similarities between health patients using random forests. In Course 4, a capstone project course, we'll compare genome sequences of COVID-19 mutations to identify potential areas a drug therapy can look to target. By the end, you'll be well on your way to discovering ways to combat disease with genome sequencing.

clos.details: Analyze and design Software Component (SWC) architecture, Ports, and Interfaces based on the AUTOSAR methodology to construct the Virtual Functional Bus (VFB) communication diagram.
Configure and operate the AUTOSAR real-time operating system (AUTOSAR OS), including task management (multitasking), scheduling, and periodic execution control using Schedule Tables and Alarms.

ATS301.description:
This course aims to provide students in the Digital Automotive Engineering program with a comprehensive understanding and hands-on competencies in the AUTOSAR Classic platform. The course centers on three fundamental pillars of modern automotive software: layered software architecture, real-time operating systems (RTOS), and diagnostic systems.
Through this course, students will:
- Understand layered AUTOSAR architecture: Learn the roles of the Application (ASW), Runtime Environment (RTE), and Basic Software (BSW), and design hardware-independent Software Components (SWC) based on the Virtual Function Bus (VFB) concept.
- Gain practical experience with AUTOSAR OS (RTOS): Configure and manage multitasking systems, including task creation, priority assignment, scheduling mechanisms, and timing control using Alarms and Schedule Tables.
- Apply basic diagnostic mechanisms: Explore international diagnostic standards (ISO 14229 – UDS) and understand the roles of DCM, DEM, and NvM modules in automotive software systems.
- Develop a practical AUTOSAR project: Use the MaaZ Edu SDK and SCons build environment to design ARXML configurations, generate RTE code, and deploy application logic on simulated or hardware platforms.
By the end of the course, students will possess both theoretical knowledge of AUTOSAR and practical skills in real-time system performance—an essential competency for ECU software engineers in the automotive industry.

BDF201.description: This course introduces blockchain technology and its applications in cryptocurrencies and decentralized finance (DeFi). It covers cryptographic primitives (hash functions, digital signatures), blockchain data structures (blocks, Merkle trees), network architecture (nodes, mempool), consensus mechanisms and security (PoW/PoS, forks, double spending, 51% attack), and the evolution from Bitcoin to smart-contract platforms. The DeFi part focuses on financial primitives and protocols such as stablecoins, decentralized exchanges and automated market makers (AMMs), liquidity pools, tokenization and NFTs, governance via DAOs, and key issues in risk management, security, and regulation. Students will practice using wallets, block explorers, and smart-contract sandboxes; analyze real-world DeFi cases and on-chain data; and propose a DeFi/FinTech solution with clear assumptions, risks, and compliance considerations.

This course has 9 modules. Each offers a different perspectives on digital technology in the strategic context. It is designed for leaders focused on implementing new ideas, staying ahead of the competition and aligning their people, data and technology to drive digital transformation. The program explores various core areas, including general cloud and Google Cloud know-how, modernizing company IT infrastructure and applications, and evoking digital transformation through data and AI/ML.

Upon completion, you will be able to recall critical cloud terminologies, recognize Google Cloud products and solutions driving digital transformation, discuss how cloud technology and data can steer innovation within organizations, and identify key changes to leverage Google Cloud products for infrastructure and application modernization.

clos.details: Describe the role of technology in the banking and financial services business, including banking products and services in the digital era, the technology inheritance, digital-first banking models and the current banking-fintech landscape.

Explain how a bank works as a technology system, including the core banking platform, database and platform architecture, availability and resilience, single customer view, integration and banking APIs, microservices, and banking data and reporting.

BFT201.description:
1. Course Objectives:
This course aims to provide learners with a comprehensive understanding of how technology is applied within modern banking systems. Students will explore the historical development of banking technology, key digital infrastructures, and core banking functions such as payments and customer interaction. The course also examines opportunities and risks arising from digital transformation in the financial sector. By the end of the course, learners will be able to analyze banking technology ecosystems and engage effectively with both technical and business stakeholders in the industry.
2. Course Content:
The course is organised in six blocks. (1) Foundations of digital banking, including the evolution of banking and its technology landscape; (2) Architecture and data, covering core banking systems, databases, and integration technologies; (3) Digital channels, such as internet/mobile banking and customer interaction across platforms; (4) Payments and operations, including card payments, interbank systems, and risk management technologies; (5) Regulation and governance, focusing on compliance, data protection, and technology management; and (6) Future trends in digital banking, supported by an applied project.
3. Activities and Teaching Methodology:
Of the 60 sessions, roughly 40 are guided lectures and case discussions and the remainder are applied workshops, project checkpoints, assessment and review. Workshops ask students to trace transactions end-to-end, read a public banking API portal, audit a real bank's cross-channel journey, map an instant payment flow, and translate a regulatory requirement into technology requirements. All technical content is delivered at conceptual and interpretive level: students read, explain and evaluate architectures and process flows; no programming, configuration or systems administration is required.

BKG303.description:
This course introduces students to the principles and techniques of investment project appraisal in both private and public sectors. It covers the critical aspects of evaluating investment opportunities, including financial modeling, risk assessment, cost-benefit analysis, and the impact of financing and taxation on investment decisions. The course aims to equip students with the analytical tools necessary to assess the viability of investment projects and make informed financial decisions.

Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
 (i) Understand and apply the fundamental principles of investment appraisal.
 (ii) Conduct financial analyses using discounted cash flow (DCF) techniques.
 (iii) Evaluate the impact of risk and uncertainty on investment decisions.
 (iv) Compare and contrast different investment appraisal methods.
 (v)Prepare comprehensive investment appraisal reports.

BPS301.description: Business Process Management (BPM) is the set of concepts, methods, and tools that help organizations define, implement, measure and improve their end-to-end processes. BPM is a combination of mature organizational transformation concepts and supporting technologies such as workflow management, process analytics, process mining, and service-oriented systems. BPM technology helps organizations become more efficient by coordinating activities, automatically allocating tasks to process participants and integrating services and applications into the process. The course is also suitable for students interested in joining IT organizations with BPM tool offerings and provides business-level education for future sales-force personnel, technical staff, and consultants

assessments.questionType: Report + PresentationTask Description:Students will work in groups of 4 or 5 and immerse themselves in an extensive analysis of a specific brand as well as the company that owns it. As this is an extensive analysis, it will involve qualitative and quantitative research, and literature/market/industry review. Students are encouraged to select a brand for which public information is readily available. Brand managers, research managers and C-level executives are supposed to be the target audience for the brand audit report. Accordingly, the report should have multiple components including Brand History and Overview, Key Challenges Facing Brand, Brand Inventory, Brand Exploratory and maybe, Brand Resonance Pyramid. Presentation:For the 20-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates to help them gain insights into the brand you have chosen. Report: Include the following sections in your report1. Brand History and Overview Summarize the evolution of the brand, including its past and present positioning.2.Key Challenges Facing Brand Explain the key challenges facing the brand and lay the foundation for the brand audit focus and outcomes.3. Brand Inventory: Brief description/summary of each item 4. Brand Exploratory: Focus Group Insights 5. Reflections and Recommendations Generate marketing recommendations that address specific branding issues.6. Appendices Notes: Students are required to:1. Obtain formal approval from their lecturer for their selected topic before beginning the assignment.2. Use AI tools to research the industry and product category of their chosen brand by:• Synthesizing and aggregating industry information• Writing a brief summary of key findings• Demonstrating comprehensive understanding of the industry prior to topic consultation• Including a clear acknowledgment of AI tool usage in the report3. Note that while AI tools may be used to gain industry insights: • Students must acknowledge all AI-generated information in their reports.• Students must demonstrate their ability to conduct the brand audit independently.• The use of AI tools is required but will not be graded separately; the quality of their completed work will be assessed as a whole.Each student will need to conduct at least one interview/survey (choice of person interviewed to be approved by the instructor) and include the full transcript of the interview in the annex section of the report.An example of a completed brand audit appears in the textbook.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the delivered chapters (1-10).
assessments.gradingGuide: Rubric: Brand Audit Group Assignment 1. Report (65%) a. Brand History and Overview (10%) Clear and concise summary of the brand’s evolution. Demonstrates understanding of brand’s past/present positioning and relevance. b. Key Challenges Facing the Brand (10%) Identifies critical, evidence-based challenges. Provides clear link to why these challenges matter for the audit. c. Brand Inventory (10%) Comprehensive and organized review of brand elements (logo, slogan, packaging, distribution, communications, etc.). Balanced qualitative and quantitative details. d. Brand Exploratory (15%) Quality of primary research (e.g., focus group, survey, interviews). Insightfulness of findings (e.g., customer perceptions, associations, experiences). Integration of findings into the brand’s situation. e. Reflections and Recommendations (10%) Creative, realistic, and well-argued recommendations. Directly address the brand challenges. Show originality, feasibility, and alignment with brand positioning. f. Literature / Market / Industry Review (5%) Incorporation of credible secondary sources (academic + industry) Shows evidence of both qualitative & quantitative research. g. Organization, Formatting, Appendices (5%) Professional structure (executive summary, headings, flow). Appendices (focus group transcript, charts, tables) add value. APA/Harvard citation style correct. 2. Presentation (25%) a. Content & Key Insights (10%) Covers all main sections of the report concisely. Highlights major insights and challenges clearly. b. Delivery & Engagement (5%) Speakers are confident, organized, and balanced in group contribution. Slides are professional, clear, and visually engaging. c. Audience Relevance (5%) Tailored for brand managers, executives, classmates. Focused on decision-making insights rather than just description. d. Time Management & Q&A (5%) Stays within 20-minute limit. Handles Q&A professionally and knowledgeably. 3. Effective usage of AI tools (10%) Students will explain how they have utilized various AI-powered tools in their assignment.
assessments.note:
Students can use AI tools/ AI-based sytems to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the industry; however, they are strongly advised to double-check all outputs. Additionally, they must demonstrate the ability to conduct a brand audit independently. Students' works will be assessed according to a rubric provided by the lecturer

 The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.questionType: Report + PresentationTask Description:Based on their Brand Audit, students will continue working with their teammates again to create one brand campaign in order to address brand’s challenges and embrace brand image. The brand campaign should follow brand voice guidelines and is able to highlight thoroughly the brand personality of the organization. For this assessment, students will practise with and apply the brand strategy model and methods to a real world brand of your choosing. Students will learn the difference between brand campaign strategies and other types of campaign strategies. Presentation:For the 20-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates.Your presentation should showcase how we are able to increase brand awareness and brand equity by using the right strategies, content and media platforms.Report:Students will apply all of the knowledge they have gained so far to create a simulated campaign again with the purpose of enhancing brand awareness and brand equity. The structure of the report will be revealed and modified during the class based on the brands the students choose to focus on.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Option1: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the delivered chapters (11-14).Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
assessments.gradingGuide: Rubric: Brand Campaign Plan Assignment (Option 1: Report + Presentation) 1. Report (65%) a. Campaign Strategy & Alignment (15%) Clear articulation of campaign objectives (awareness, equity, positioning). Strong alignment between campaign goals and the brand’s challenges, image, and personality. Distinguishes a brand campaign strategy from other campaign types. b. Application of Brand Strategy Models (15%) Effective use of models (e.g., Keller’s CBBE, Aaker’s brand identity model, resonance pyramid). Shows how theory is translated into actionable strategy. Demonstrates understanding of brand equity concepts. c. Creativity & Brand Voice (10%) Campaign reflects brand personality and adheres to brand voice guidelines. Innovative ideas, engaging storytelling, and fresh approaches. Realistic yet distinctive in positioning the brand. d. Content & Media Plan (10%) Clear articulation of proposed content types (visuals, messaging, storytelling). Justification of chosen media platforms (digital, social, traditional). Integration across platforms for consistency and reach. e. Feasibility & Recommendations (10%) Campaign plan is realistic given resources (time, budget, context). Recommendations are actionable and defendable. Risks and limitations considered. f. Report Structure & Research Support (5%) Logical, professional structure (executive summary, sections, flow). Evidence from qualitative/quantitative data, industry sources, or case examples. Correct referencing (APA/Harvard). 2. Presentation (30%) a. Content & Insight Delivery (10%) Highlights the key elements of the campaign strategy. Shows how the campaign enhances brand awareness and equity. Clear link to research and theory. b. Creativity & Engagement (10%) Presentation design is engaging, professional, and on-brand. Delivery captures audience interest and communicates brand personality. Strong group collaboration with balanced participation c. Relevance & Audience Tailoring (5%) Tailored for an executive-level audience (brand managers, C-suite). Focuses on decision-making insights and practical outcomes. d. Time Management & Q&A (5%) Presentation flows well and stays within 20 minutes. Q&A handled confidently, showing strong grasp of the material. 3. Effective usage of AI tools (5%) Students will explain how they have utilized various AI-powered tools in their assignment.

assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Required Campaign Components'Students will collaborate in teams of four to six to complete this assignment. Each group will select an existing product or service from a small business, startup, or non-profit organization (NGO) and develop a creative advertising campaign plan that demonstrates both strategic thinking and creative execution.The campaign should be grounded in a clearly defined communication problem and supported by relevant consumer insights. All creative elements must align with the overall strategy and reinforce a unified brand message across platforms.Each campaign must include the following elements:1. Brand OverviewBrief background of the organization, product/service, target market, and competitive context.2. Communication Problem Identification and ObjectivesA clear articulation of the key communication challenge or opportunity, followed by clearly stated communication objectives the campaign aims to achieve.3. Consumer Insight DevelopmentInsight(s) derived from consumer behavior, attitudes, motivations, or tensions relevant to the brand and the communication problem.4. Key Message and Big IdeaA concise key message and a compelling Big Idea that guides all creative executions.5. Media selection and TacticsA cohesive explanation of the campaign’s media selection and tactics, including:- Platform and channel selections- Specific tactics implemented on each platform- Rationale explaining how strategy, media choices, and tactics work together to achieve campaign objectives6. Timeline and BudgetA realistic implementation schedule and a high-level budget allocation.7. Evaluation MethodsKey performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics used to assess campaign effectiveness.Creative DeliverablesIn addition to the creative advertising campaign plan, students must produce sample creative materials that bring the campaign to life. Each group is required to submit at least three of the following creative executions (including but not limited to):- Print or social media advertisements- Posters or digital display advertisements- Short videos or storyboards- Audio clips or radio scripts- Mock-ups for outdoor, mobile, or experiential formatsAll deliverables must demonstrate coherent creative execution, consistent tone and visual identity, and clear alignment with the campaign strategy and Big Idea.PresentationEach group will deliver an in-class presentation presenting their creative advertising campaign.

CCO201.description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to corporate communications and public relations: it is for anyone with an interest in corporate communication, or anyone seeking to understand the growing importance of communication for corporations. Corporations increasingly need communication to survive, as they need to entertain relations with a variety of stakeholders to prosper. This includes not only external factors to the organization – customers, governments and civil ociety organizations, but also stakeholders within corporations themselves, such as employees, managers and investors.

The first weeks of the course focus on the basics of corporate communication: what is it, and what are its historical roots? This is important, as it demonstrates how the position of communication is increasingly considered to be managerial function – and as such should be involved in the key decision-making processes. After these introductory weeks, we turn to two core theories of corporate communication: stakeholder theory and corporate identity. These form the basis for much of the more specific and applied topics covered in the following weeks. 

In addition, students will be introduced to the use of AI in corporate communications. This includes how to leverage AI tools for stakeholder analysis, media monitoring, content creation, and campaign evaluation, as well as how to address ethical and cultural considerations when adopting AI. In the last two weeks before the midterm exam, we discuss how corporations can construct communication campaigns – which will be useful as you will be tasked with creating your own communication campaign during the course. Students will also explore how AI can support the design and execution of such campaigns through audience segmentation, trend analysis, and strategic messaging assistance. After the midterm exam, we tackle specific topics of corporate communication, such as employee communications, how corporations interact with media and journalists, and how corporations should communicate in times of crisis.

完成本课程后，学习者能够系统性地阐述中国地理、民族、人口、宗教、经济、政治、教育、科学技术、哲学思想、风俗习惯、文学艺术及对外文化交流等方面的核心内容，并能够解释这些领域在历史与现代发展进程中的辩证关系。

学习者能够运用所学知识，科学、多维度地分析和评价中国的文化社会现象；能够进行与中国相关主题的研究、小组讨论和展示；同时能够熟练使用各类参考文献资料，服务于对中国问题的深入了解。

【自主与责任目标】

CCS401.description:
一、知识内容要求 本课程知识内容围绕“汉语学习辅助+中国认知构建”展开，兼顾基础性、实用性和趣味性，贴合留学生汉语水平梯度，避免复杂晦涩表述，重点要求掌握以下核心知识，同时强化汉语词汇、句式的积累与运用，实现“学知识、练汉语”的双重目标： 
（一）基础国情知识 
1. 地理与行政：掌握中国的国土面积、地理位置、主要地形地貌、重要河流湖泊等基础地理知识；了解中国的省级行政区划、首都及主要城市，能运用汉语说出至少5个省份、3个主要城市的名称及简要特点，消除因地理背景缺失导致的汉语交际障碍。 
2. 人口与民族：了解中国的人口总量、分布特点，掌握“汉族”“少数民族”等核心词汇；熟悉主要少数民族的分布、代表性文化习俗（如服饰、节日），能使用简单汉语句子描述不同民族的特色，理解中国多民族共生的国情。
（二）历史与文化知识 
1. 历史脉络：了解中国历史发展的基本阶段，掌握夏、商、周、秦、汉、唐、宋、明、清等主要朝代的名称及核心特征，熟悉丝绸之路、郑和下西洋等重要历史事件，能运用汉语简单叙述关键历史节点的意义。 
2. 传统文化：掌握中国传统节日（春节、中秋节、端午节等）的时间、习俗及相关汉语表达（如“团圆”“粽子”“春联”）；了解传统思想（儒家、道家核心理念）、传统艺术（书法、国画、京剧）、传统饮食（八大菜系、特色小吃）的基础内容，积累相关汉语词汇和常用句式
（三）当代社会与生活知识 
1. 政治与外交：了解中国的基本政治制度、国家机构，掌握“人民代表大会”“中国共产党”“外交政策”等基础词汇；熟悉中国的外交原则、主要国际交往成果，能使用简单汉语谈论中国的国际地位。
2. 经济与科技：了解中国当代经济发展的基本状况、主要成就（如数字经济、高铁、新能源），掌握“经济发展”“科技创新”“互联网”等相关汉语词汇；熟悉中国的科技发展现状，能运用汉语简单描述身边的科技成果。 
3. 生活与习俗：掌握中国日常社交礼仪（问候、见面、告别、餐桌礼仪）的汉语表达及行为规范；了解中国的教育体系、医疗保障、交通出行等日常生活相关知识，能运用汉语解决简单的生活交流问题，快速适应中国生活。
（四）汉语学习辅助知识 结合课程内容，积累与国情、文化相关的汉语词汇、固定句式和常用表达，掌握中国特色词汇的准确含义及用法，能区分易混淆词汇；了解汉语在不同国情场景（如介绍家乡、谈论节日、描述社会现象）中的运用差异，为汉语听、说、读、写能力提升奠定基础。 
二、能力培养要求 本课程以“汉语应用能力”为核心，结合中国概况知识的学习，重点培养留学生的汉语综合运用能力、跨文化交际能力和自主学习能力，实现“能听懂、能表达、能交流、能应用”的目标，同时兼顾学术探究能力的初步培养：
（一）汉语综合运用能力 
1. 听力能力：能听懂关于中国概况的简单汉语讲解、对话、新闻片段，理解课程相关的基础词汇、句式和核心信息，能应对日常国情相关的听力场景（如介绍中国节日、讲解中国地理）。 
2. 口语表达能力：能运用汉语简单介绍中国的地理、节日、习俗、当代发展等内容，能围绕课程知识点进行简单对话、提问和讨论；能清晰表达自己对中国国情、文化的看法，纠正口语表达中的常见错误，提升表达的流畅度和准确性。 
3. 阅读能力：能阅读关于中国概况的简单汉语短文、图片说明、宣传材料，理解文章大意和核心信息，能从中提取关键知识点（如时间、地点、事件、特点），积累汉语阅读经验。 
4. 写作能力：能运用课程所学词汇和句式，书写简单的汉语短文（如介绍中国节日、描述中国城市、谈谈对中国的印象），做到语句通顺、逻辑清晰，能准确表达自己的想法，字数达到课程要求。
（二）跨文化交际与认知能力 
1. 能了解中国文化与自身母语文化的差异，尊重中国的风俗习惯、价值观念，消除跨文化误解，培养多元文化意识。 
2. 能运用课程所学知识和汉语表达，与中国人进行日常交流、文化沟通，能应对简单的跨文化交际场景（如节日问候、习俗交流），提升跨文化交际的自信心和有效性。 
3. 能通过课程学习，客观认识中国的国情、文化和社会发展，理解中国的思维方式和行为逻辑，形成对中国的全面、正确认知。
（三）自主学习与探究能力 
1. 能主动利用课程资源（课本、课件、视频、课外读物），自主学习中国概况相关知识，积累汉语词汇和表达，养成自主学习的习惯。 
2. 能针对自己感兴趣的中国国情、文化话题，主动查阅资料、提问探究，尝试用汉语整理和表达探究结果，初步培养学术研究能力。 
3. 能结合自身汉语学习需求，将中国概况知识与汉语学习结合起来，主动运用所学知识解决汉语学习和日常生活中的问题，提升学习的主动性和针对性。
三、学习成果 通过本课程的学习，留学生需在知识、能力、认知三个层面达成以下成果，实现“汉语能力提升”与“中国认知深化”的双重目标，为后续汉语学习和在中国的生活、学习奠定基础： 
（一）知识成果 
1. 熟练掌握中国概况的核心知识，包括地理、人口、民族、历史、文化、当代社会、日常生活等方面的基础内容，能准确记忆相关汉语词汇和核心知识点。 
2. 积累至少200个与中国概况相关的汉语词汇、30个常用句式，能准确理解和运用这些词汇、句式，区分易混淆表达，掌握中国特色词汇的含义和用法。 
3. 了解中国的基本国情和文化精髓，熟悉中国的社会规则、社交礼仪和生活习俗，能准确区分中国文化与自身母语文化的核心差异。
（二）能力成果 
1. 汉语综合能力显著提升：能听懂关于中国概况的简单汉语讲解和对话，能流畅进行日常国情相关的口语交流，能阅读简单的国情类汉语短文，能写出语句通顺、逻辑清晰的短文，汉语表达的准确性和流畅度明显提高。 
2. 具备基本的跨文化交际能力：能尊重中国的文化和习俗，能运用汉语与中国人进行有效的日常交流，能应对简单的跨文化交际场景，有效减少跨文化误解，提升跨文化沟通的有效性。 
3. 具备自主学习和探究能力：能自主查阅中国概况相关资料，主动积累汉语词汇和表达，能针对感兴趣的话题进行简单探究，能将课程知识与汉语学习、日常生活结合起来，形成自主学习的能力和习惯。
（三）认知与情感成果 
1. 形成对中国的全面、客观认知，了解中国的发展成就和文化魅力，消除对中国的误解，增强对中国文化的兴趣和认同感。 
2. 培养多元文化包容心，尊重不同国家、不同民族的文化差异，树立正确的跨文化观念，为后续在中国的学习、生活和国际交流奠定良好的认知基础。 
3. 激发汉语学习的兴趣和动力，明确汉语学习与中国概况认知的关联，愿意主动运用汉语了解中国、传播中国文化，成为中外文化交流的桥梁。

CDP301.description:
The Circuit Design Project course aims to provide students with both theoretical understanding and practical experience in modern electronic circuit design. By the end of the course, students will be able to:
- Understand and apply the modern electronic circuit design process — from requirement analysis, schematic design, and PCB layout to to manufacturing and hardware validation.
- Demonstrate proficiency in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools such as KiCad, Altium or Cadence OrCAD (optional), capable of designing and verifying single-layer and double-layer PCBs.
- Integrate hardware and firmware (using MCU STM32/Nucleo; ESP32/ESP8266, Arduino...) to test and validate their hardware designs and circuit functionality.
- Develop key engineering competencies including teamwork, communication, documentation, and project management aligned with industry practice.
- Cultivate creativity and innovation by designing functional and application-oriented electronic products, with potential extensions in IoT, sensing, control, or embedded systems.
CDP301.studentTasks:
Students are expected to:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Attend and participate actively in lectures, labs, and discussions according to the weekly schedule
- Complete all project milestones, including: 
- Collaborate effectively in teams, including task allocation, maintaining project logs, and performing peer reviews of other teams’ designs
- Engage in self-directed learning by exploring components, IoT modules, and best practices in EMC/EMI and layout optimization
- Deliver and present the Final Project, including a functional PCB prototype, working firmware, a comprehensive technical report, and a live or recorded demonstration

CEA201.description: This course in an introduction to computer architecture and organization. It will cover topics in both the physical design of the computer (organization) and the logical design of the computer (architecture). The main contents include the organization of a simple stored-program computer: CPU, busses and memory; Instruction sets, machine code, and assembly language; Conventions for assembly language generated by compilers; Floating-point number representation; Hardware organization of simple processors; Address translation and virtual memory; Very introductory examples of input/output devices, interrupt handling and multi-tasking systems.Chapter covered: Computer Evolution and Performance; A Top-Level View of Computer Function and Interconnection; Cache Memory; Internal Memory; External Memory; Input/Output; Operating System Support; Instruction Sets: Characteristics and Functions; Processor Structure and Function; Reduced Instruction Set Computers; Instruction-Level Parallelism and Superscalar Processors; Parallel Processing; Multicore Computers.
