clos.details: Demonstrate an ability to integrate cross-disciplinary knowledge (business and technology), handle complexity, and plan and carry out advanced tasks independently and as a group member within specified time limits.
Use appropriate market research methodology to identify market problems, validate demand, and propose a digital solution that is both technically feasible and commercially viable.
Design, implement, and test a software system aligned with stated business requirements, using sound software engineering principles: requirements, architecture, iterative development, and testing.
Develop critical thinking, creative problem-solving, and management capabilities; analyze marketing, operational, and financial aspects of the digital product in theory and practice.
Apply project-management principles to coordinate an interdisciplinary team and deliver a working digital product within schedule and quality constraints.
Write, present and defend the thesis—including the business case and technical design—according to well-defined academic and professional criteria, with correct referencing.
Produce a feasible, deployable digital product or near-production MVP that demonstrates real-world entrepreneurial and engineering value and supports actual or potential business operation.

GRC490.description: GRC490 is an integrative capstone experience bridging Business Administration and Software Engineering. Interdisciplinary teams identify a genuine market problem, validate the business opportunity, design and build a functioning, deployable digital product, and defend both its business viability and technical implementation. Each team is guided by two co-supervisors—one from each faculty—and each student is assessed individually before a mixed committee.
GRC490.studentTasks: 1. Form an interdisciplinary team and select a project requiring both a business case and a working software product.2. Divide and schedule work clearly across business and technical roles.3. Attend at least 80% of scheduled supervisor meetings to remain eligible for defense.4. Conduct primary and secondary market research.5. Produce all required reports and a functioning, deployable software product through iterative development and testing.6. Defend the business viability and technical implementation individually before the evaluation committee.7. Academic dishonesty disqualifies the entire team from defense.
GRC490.tools: Business analysis: market research platforms, Excel/Google Sheets, survey tools.Design: Figma, draw.io, Lucidchart or equivalent.Development: appropriate IDE, Git/GitHub, CI/CD pipeline and deployment platform.Project management: Jira, Trello, Notion or equivalent.
GRC490.note: Delivered and assessed entirely in English. All business reports, technical documents, thesis, slides and oral defense must be in English. Technical documents should follow applicable international software-engineering standards (IEEE 830, IEEE 1016 or equivalent). Recommended team size: 6–7 students (3–4 SE + 2–3 BIZ).

GRH491.description:
-Objective:
The objective of the Graduation Thesis is to demonstrate students' profound knowledge and understanding of a specific topic in relation to Hospitality Management and relate it to a wider perspective, in a more practical business setting. 

Upon completion of the course, the student shall be able to: 
1. Demonstrate an ability to integrate knowledge and handle complexity, and to plan and carry out advanced tasks independently and as a group member, within specified time limits
2. Use appropriate research methodology to identify problems and suggest suitable, more sustainable solutions to those issues
3. Develop a more critical and creative thinking both theoretically and practically
4. Write, present and defend the thesis fulfilling academic criteria; correctly referencing relevant literature and other materials, which reflect the student’s academic and non-academic development throughout the whole process

-Description:
The Graduation Thesis is an integrative experience that brings together various components of the undergraduate marketing studies in a more applied setting and under a new perspective. clos.details: Achieving depth and breadth of knowledge: A systematic understanding of knowledge, including, where appropriate, relevant knowledge outside the field and/or discipline, and a critical awareness of current problems and/or new insights, much of which is at, or informed by, the forefront of their academic discipline, field of study, or area of professional practice;
Applying established techniques of research and inquiry are used to create and interpret knowledge in the discipline

Applying a critical evaluation of current research and advanced research in the discipline or area of professional competence and treatment of complex issues and judgments based on established principles and techniques;
Applying knowledge: Competence in the research process by applying an existing body of knowledge in critically analyzing a new question or specific problem or issue in a new setting.
Planning and using adequate methods to conduct qualified tasks in given frameworks and to evaluate this work
Creating, analyzing, and critically evaluating different technical/architectural solutions.
Being able to critically and systematically integrate knowledge.
Being able to clearly present and discuss the conclusions as well as the knowledge and arguments that form the basis for these findings in written and spoken English.
Identifing the issues that must be addressed within the framework of the specific thesis in order to take into consideration all relevant dimensions of sustainable development.
Creating a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.

GRT491.description:
It enables students to further their knowledge and skills in tourism management and related topics which they have found to be especially interesting or beneficial to them.

As part of the course, students will learn about all aspects of the process of developing and carrying out the graduation thesis and gain an understanding of the standards and expectations needed to successfully complete their dissertation. This thesis project will be completed by a group of 4-6 students, however each student will defend the thesis individually in front of a thesis committee. Each group of students will be supported by a supervisor, who will provide them with essential guidance in conducting a research, writing a thesis in a formal format and defending their arguments in front of the examination board. 

The thesis' topic should concern with the following areas: Tourism and Customer Satisfaction, Tourism Marketing and Destination Management, Tourism Management, Service Quality Management, Strategic Management in the Tourism Industry, Human Resource Management, Tourism sustainable development.

(5) Defense individually work in front of examination board

GSF301.description:
International Sea Freight Fowarding is a practice‑oriented course that equips student with the knowledge and skills to manage the full life cycle of sea freight operations. It focuses on how sea ports and terminals, freight forwarders, and shipping lines, and consignors work together to move cargo safely, quickly, and profitably in today’s global supply chains

Throughout the course, real cases and examples will illustrate how sea freignt fowarding supports trade and logistics development in Vietnam, helping learners see clear links between theory and local industry practice. By the end of the module, students will be able to design and evaluate sea freight solutions, communicate effectively with international partners, and position yourself for careers with shipping lines, logistics service providers, and sea port operators.

clos.details:
Hiểu được những kiến thức cơ bản về khái niệm, đối tượng, nguồn gốc, phương pháp nghiên cứu và ý nghĩa của môn học tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh 
Understand the basic knowledge of the concepts, objectives, origins, research methods, and significance of the Ho Chi Minh Thought course

Phân tích được bối cảnh lịch sử Việt Nam từ cuối thế kỷ XIX đến thế kỷ XXI, nguồn gốc, cơ sở, quá trình hình thành và phát triển tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh. Hiểu được sự vận dụng của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam trong cách mạng dân tộc dân chủ nhân dân và trong cách mạng xã hội chủ nghĩa
Analyze the historical context of Vietnam from the late 19th century to the 21st century, as well as the origins, basis, formation, and development of Ho Chi Minh Thought. Understand the Communist Party of Vietnam’s application of Ho Chi Minh Thought in the people’s democratic revolution and the socialist revolution

Nắm được về hệ thống quan điểm tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về các vấn đề độc lập dân tộc và chủ nghĩa xã hội, đại đoàn kết dân tộc và đoàn kết quốc tế, xây dựng Đảng và Nhà nước, đạo đức, văn hóa, con người 
Understanding Ho Chi Minh's system of ideological views on national independence and socialism, the great unity bloc and international solidarity, the construction of the Party and State, ethics, culture, people

Hiểu được vai trò nền tảng lý luận của Chủ nghĩa Mác-Lênin, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh đối với đường lối của Đảng, Nhà nước.
Understand the role of Marxism-Leninism and Ho Chi Minh's ideology as the ideological foundation for Vietnamese Communist Party and State's guidelines

HCM202.description:
Giới thiệu/Mô tả môn học: Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là kết tinh của truyền thống hàng nghìn năm dựng nước và giữ nước của dân tộc Việt Nam. Trên nền tảng đó, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh đã gạn lọc các hạt giống trí tuệ của phương Đông, phương Tây, vận dụng sáng tạo và phát triển chủ nghĩa Mác - Lênin vào điều kiện cụ thể của nước ta. Khái quát lại bản chất khoa học này, Đảng ta khẳng định: Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là một hệ thống quan điểm toàn diện và sâu sắc về những vấn đề cơ bản của cách mạng Việt Nam, kết quả của sự vận dụng và phát triển sáng tạo chủ nghĩa Mác - Lênin vào điều kiện cụ thể của nước ta, kế thừa và phát triển các giá trị truyền thống tốt đẹp của dân tộc, tiếp thu tinh hoa văn hoá nhân loại. Mục tiêu của tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là hướng tới giải phóng dân tộc - giải phóng xã hội - giải phóng giai cấp - giải phóng con người. Do đó, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là tài sản tinh thần vô cùng to lớn và quý giá của Đảng và dân tộc ta, mãi mãi soi đường cho sự nghiệp cách mạng của nhân dân ta giành thắng lợi.

Course Introduction / Description: Ho Chi Minh Ideology is the crystallization of the thousand-year-old traditions of national construction and defense of the Vietnamese people. On that basis, Ho Chi Minh Ideology has selectively absorbed the intellectual quintessence of the East and the West, and creatively applied and developed Marxism-Leninism to the specific conditions of Vietnam. Summarizing this scientific nature, our Party affirms: Ho Chi Minh Ideology is a comprehensive and profound system of views on fundamental issues of the Vietnamese revolution, the result of the creative application and development of Marxism-Leninism to the specific conditions of our country, inheriting and developing the fine traditional values of the nation, and absorbing the cultural quintessence of humanity. Its goal aims at national liberation, social liberation, class liberation, and human liberation. Therefore, Ho Chi Minh Ideology is an immensely large and precious spiritual asset of our Party and nation, forever illuminating the path for our people's revolutionary cause to achieve victory.

Mục tiêu môn học:
- Về kiến thức: Sinh viên hiểu được những kiến thức cơ bản về khái niệm, nguồn gốc, quá trình hình thành và phát triển tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; những nội dung cơ bản về tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; sự vận dụng của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam trong cách mạng dân tộc dân chủ nhân dân và trong cách mạng xã hội chủ nghĩa.
- Về kỹ năng: Hình thành cho sinh viên khả năng tư duy độc lập, phân tích, đánh giá, vận dụng sáng tạo tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh vào giải quyết các vấn đề trong thực tiễn đời sống, học tập và công tác.
- Về thái độ: Sinh viên được nâng cao bản lĩnh chính trị, yêu nước, trung thành với mục tiêu, lý tưởng độc lập dân tộc gắn liền chủ nghĩa xã hội; nhận thức được vai trò, giá trị của tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh đối với Đảng và dân tộc Việt Nam; thấy được trách nhiệm của bản thân trong việc học tập, rèn luyện để góp phần vào xây dựng và bảo vệ Tổ quốc.

Course Objectives:
- Knowledge: Students understand the basic concepts, origins, formation, and development of Ho Chi Minh Ideology; the core contents of Ho Chi Minh Ideology; and its application by the Communist Party of Vietnam in the people’s democratic revolution and in the socialist revolution.
- Skills: Students develop the ability to think independently, analyze, evaluate, and creatively apply Ho Chi Minh Ideology to solve practical problems in daily life, academic work, and professional activities.
- Attitudes: Students strengthen political courage and patriotism, remain loyal to the goal and ideal of national independence associated with socialism; recognize the role and value of Ho Chi Minh Ideology for the Party and the Vietnamese nation; and understand their personal responsibility in learning and self-improvement to contribute to national construction and defense.

Nội dung môn học: Học phần bao gồm 6 chương, cung cấp cho sinh viên kiến thức cơ bản về Khái niệm, đối tượng, phương pháp nghiên cứu và ý nghĩa học tập môn tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; Về cơ sở, quá trình hình thành và phát triển tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về: Độc lập dân tộc và chủ nghĩa xã hội; Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam và Nhà nước của nhân dân, do nhân dân, vì nhân dân; Đại đoàn kết dân tộc và đoàn kết quốc tế; Văn hóa, đạo đức, con người.
Content of the course: The course consists of 6 chapters, providing students with basic knowledge on Concept, object of study, research methodology, and significance of studying Ho Chi Minh Ideology; Basis, formation, and development process of Ho Chi Minh Ideology; Ho Chi Minh Ideology on: National independence and socialism; the Communist Party of Vietnam and the State of the people, by the people, for the people; Great national unity and international solidarity; Culture, ethics, and human beings.

Phương pháp dạy học: Thuyết giảng và kết hợp trình chiếu các slide bài giảng. Hướng dẫn, giao bài tập đề tài theo nhóm. Tổ chức và hướng dẫn sinh viên thảo luận nhóm, thuyết trình và thực hiện sản phẩm sáng tạo (tham khảo và ứng dụng phần mềm AI một cách có trách nhiệm).
Teaching methods: Giving lectures and slide presentations. Guiding and assigning group projects. Organizing and guiding students in group discussions, presentations, and the development of creative products (with the responsible and ethical use of AI tools).
HCM202.studentTasks:
Nhiệm vụ của sinh viên:
 - Tham gia tối thiểu 80% thời lượng môn học và tham dự đủ các buổi lên lớp, thảo luận theo quy định. 
 - Phải có Giáo trình Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh (dành cho bậc đại học hệ không chuyên lý luận chính trị) do Bộ Giáo dục và Đào tạo ban hành.
 - Phải nghiên cứu giáo trình trước, chuẩn bị các ý kiến để đề xuất khi nghe giảng. Chuẩn bị thảo luận và đọc, sưu tầm các tư liệu có liên quan đến nội dung môn học.
 - Thực hiện đầy đủ các yêu cầu của giảng viên khi học trên lớp cũng như các chủ đề sinh viên tự chuẩn bị trước khi đến lớp.
 - Chỉ sử dụng máy tính xách tay trong lớp cho mục đích học tập.
 - Ứng dụng AI một cách có trách nhiệm, đạo đức trong quá trình học tập và thực tiễn.
 
 Student's Tasks:
 - Attend at least 80% of class hours and participate in discussions as required. 
 - Own the Ho Chi Minh's thought (Sửa lại từ sai lệch chính trị "Ho Chi Minh Ideology") textbook (for non-majors in political theory - Nâng cấp học thuật từ cụm "non-politics majored students") issued by the Ministry of Education and Training.
 - Study the textbook in advance, prepare ideas to propose during lectures. Prepare for discussions and read, collect materials related to the course content.
 - Fulfill tasks given by the instructor in class as well as topics required to be prepared (Sửa lại ngữ pháp cho chuẩn mực từ cụm "needed to prepare") in advance.
 - Use laptops in class only for learning purposes.
 - Apply AI responsibly and ethically in both learning and practice.

Qua môn học sinh viên được trang bị kiến thức về quá trình hình thành và phát triển của Mỹ thuật Việt Nam và Thế giới, Những kiến thức cơ bản về thành tựu và đặc điểm của mỹ thuật cổ đại, mỹ thuật Phục hưng, những trường phái mỹ thuật lớn góp phần làm thay đổi diện mạo của mỹ thuật cũng được đề cập đến trong môn học này. 
Giới thiệu những trung tâm mỹ thuật tiêu biểu của châu Á như: Ấn Độ, Trung Quốc, Nhật Bản,… tạo điều kiện để sinh viên có cái nhìn tổng quát về mỹ thuật thế giới, đặc biệt là những thành tựu mỹ thuật tiêu biểu.

HOD101.description:
Lịch sử Design là một khoa học nghiên cứu về sự ra đời và phát triển của Design cũng những yếu tố cơ bản của sự phát triển đó. 
Lịch sử Design là môn học có mục đích nhằm giải thích Design như một hiện tượng xã hội và hiện tượng lịch sử.
Nội dung của môn học là những cột mốc của những sự kiện, sự hình thành các hãng, các công ty, các nhà thiết kế, các sản phẩm và các phong cách đã tạo nên dấu ấn Design. Môn học giúp sinh viên có một cách tiếp cận với những hình thái biểu hiện của thiết kế và cung cấp cho họ những đặc điểm và phương pháp cần thiết để xác định các sản phẩm thiết kế.

HOD102c.description: The course "History of Design" explores the formation and evolution of design through various historical periods, from the Stone Age to contemporary movements. Situated at the intersection of art and science, the course provides students with a deep understanding of shifts in style, technology, and aesthetic perspectives over time, fostering an awareness of the cultural and social values that shape design.The course aims to equip students with foundational knowledge of the history and progression of design schools, while encouraging analytical and critical thinking within a historical context. Consequently, students can leverage these historical insights to identify, evaluate, and apply appropriate design elements to their future projects.

HOD402.description:
The digital landscape is evolving at an unprecedented rate with unknown threats lurking around every corner. Cybersecurity resilience in the modern world cannot be just an addon - it's a necessity. Organizations must build cybersecurity resilience, and offensive security professionals like Ethical Hackers and Penetration Testers can help proactively discover unknown threats and address them before cybercriminals do.
Target Audience This course is designed to prepare learners with the Ethical Hacker skillset. Learners will become proficient in the art of scoping, executing, and reporting on vulnerability assessments, while recommending mitigation strategies. By using an engaging gamified narrative throughout the course, with real-world inspired hands-on practice labs, learners develop essential workforce readiness skills to lay a solid foundation in offensive security.
After completing this course, learners can enter cybersecurity careers, either on the offensive security side as ethical hackers or penetration testers, or on the defensive security side by understanding the mindset and tactics of threat actors, while implementing security controls and monitoring, analyzing, and responding to current security threats.

HRM201c.description:
This specialization provides a robust introduction to the key principles, policies, and practices of human resource management. The specialization begins with a foundational course that considers alternative approaches to managing human resources, provides a background to the U.S. legal context in which employees are hired, fired, rewarded, and managed, and outlines the different reasons that people are motivated to work. The remaining three courses tackle three core areas that all managers should understand: hiring employees, evaluating their performance, and rewarding them. Throughout the courses, an accessible, scientific approach is embraced such that best practices and practical tips are informed by research, but presented in accessible, applied ways. 
Upon completing the specialization, learners will have a deeper understanding of what works in the workplace, including a toolkit of best practices for hiring, managing, and rewarding employees.

Human Resource (HR) professionals are crucial to an organization's success, playing an essential role in recruitment and management of right candidates and talents, policy development, and fostering a positive work environment. Pursuing a career in HR enables individuals to significantly contribute to an organization's overall achievements.

This program is meticulously designed to prepare aspiring HR professionals. It encompasses five modules, offering a diverse array of engaging videos, interactive activities, assessments, and peer-reviewed projects aimed at enhancing professional expertise and providing a comprehensive understanding of Human Resource Management (HRM) fundamentals.

Upon completion of this program, students will understand how to:

- Recruit, select, and onboard new employees effectively.
- Develop and implement employee policies and procedures that align with organizational objectives.
- Foster a positive work culture and enhance employee engagement.
- Understand and navigate legal and ethical considerations in HR.

Graduates of this program will receive a certificate from Coursera and gain the requisite knowledge and skills to excel in the HR field. Additionally, they will be prepared to undertake the HRCI Associate Professional in Human Resources (aPHR) certification exam, distinguishing themselves as qualified HR professionals.

assessments.note: Phương thức thực hiện và nộp bàiNhóm sinh viên hoàn thành bài tiểu luận tại nhà và nộp file điện tử theo quy định; Sau khi nộp bài, các nhóm sẽ thuyết trình về dự án của mình trước lớp và thực hiện vấn đáp cá nhân.Sử dụng AI: Khuyến khích sinh viên sử dụng các công cụ AI để hỗ trợ quá trình nghiên cứu ở giai đoạn tìm kiếm và tổng hợp thông tin. Sinh viên cần lưu lại các câu lệnh (prompts) đã sử dụng, đồng thời trình bày và giải thích cách AI đã hỗ trợ như thế nào trong bài làm của mình. Tuy nhiên, phần đánh giá, phân tích vấn đề và đề xuất giải pháp phải là kết quả của sự tư duy độc lập của sinh viên, dựa trên kiến thức và khả năng của các thành viên trong nhóm.

clos.details: Nắm được những kiến thức cơ bản về sự hình thành và phát triển của một số nhà nước điển hình trên thế giới và nhà nước Việt Nam qua các thời kỳ lịch sử
Giải thích được các yếu tố tác động, các cách thức tổ chức bộ máy nhà nước và hệ thống pháp luật trên thế giới và ở Việt Nam qua các thời kỳ lịch sử.
Phân tích được những ưu điểm và hạn chế của tổ chức bộ máy nhà nước và pháp luật trên thế giới và ở Việt Nam qua các thời kỳ lịch sử

Vận dụng các kiến thức lý luận để lý giải, đánh giá các hiện tượng về nhà nước và pháp luật trong lịch sử và trong đời sống hiện tại, dự báo được sự phát triển của nhà nước và pháp luật trong tương lai

Có khả năng làm việc độc lập hoặc làm việc theo nhóm liên quan đến vấn đề chuyên môn của môn học và sử dụng hiệu quả công nghệ cả trong trong học tập, nghiên cứu và ứng dụng kiến thức lịch sử, pháp luật
Có thái độ trân trọng, tinh thần trách nhiệm trong việc gìn giữ và phát huy các giá trị văn hóa, chính trị, pháp lý truyền thống của nhân loại và Việt Nam.

HSL101.description: Học phần này cung cấp một hệ thống kiến thức về bối cảnh lịch sử, quá trình hình thành và phát triển của nhà nước và pháp luật, đặc điểm hình thành và phát triển của nhà nước và pháp luật tại Việt Nam qua các giai đoạn lịch sử, từ thời Văn Lang, Âu Lạc cho đến các triều đại phong kiến, thời kỳ Pháp thuộc và giai đoạn từ năm 1945 đến nay. Người học cũng sẽ học về lịch sử nhà nước và pháp luật trên thế giới qua các thời kỳ lịch sử. Trên cơ sở đó, người học có thể rút ra những bài học kinh nghiệm quý báu, từ đó lý giải các vấn đề pháp luật và nhà nước hiện đại trong dòng chảy lịch sử chung. Bên cạnh đó, học phần giúp người học nâng cao tinh thần trách nhiệm trong việc gìn giữ và phát huy các giá trị văn hóa, chính trị, pháp lý truyền thống của nhân loại và Việt Nam.

- Sinh viên có trách nhiệm làm tất cả các bài tập, câu hỏi, bài tập do giảng viên/người hướng dẫn giao trên lớp hoặc ở nhà và nộp đúng hạn.

assessments.gradingGuide: Each team have 45 minutes for presentation. Evaluate the final presentation, based on what the teams introduce, share, and demonstrate their final report, mainly focus on: - Phase 1: Risk Identification & Assessment 20% - Phase 2: Mitigation Planning 25% - Phase 3: Response & Recovery 30% - Presentation: 10% - Team working: 15%
assessments.note:
1. Project Implementation: 
- Mode: Students work in assigned teams (3-5 members) to develop a comprehensive Risk Management Framework for a simulated enterprise of their choice (e.g., FinTech startup, healthcare provider, e-commerce platform).
- Project Scope: The project is scaffolded throughout the semester, with deliverables aligning with lecture topics:
 + Phase 1: Risk Identification & Assessment: Define the enterprise, its critical assets, and conduct a qualitative risk assessment.
 + Phase 2: Mitigation Planning: Develop policies and select security controls to treat identified risks, including a cost-benefit analysis.
 + Phase 3: Response & Recovery: Create core components of a resilient framework: a Business Impact Analysis (BIA), Business Continuity Plan (BCP), Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP), and a Computer Incident Response Team (CIRT) plan.
- AI Integration: Students are required to use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) for specific, defined tasks such as brainstorming threat scenarios, critiquing their plan's alignment with standards like NIST or ISO 27001, and simulating attacker/auditor perspectives. All AI-generated content must be critically evaluated and integrated with proper justification.

2. Final Project Portfolio
A consolidated written report (20-30 pages) that serves as the complete Risk Management Framework, including:
- Executive Summary & Problem Context: A clear description of the simulated enterprise and the business environment it operates in.
- Comprehensive Risk Analysis: Detailed identification of assets, threats, vulnerabilities, and the assessed impact/likelihood of risks.
- Proposed Mitigation Strategy: A detailed plan outlining selected technical and managerial controls, prioritized based on a cost-benefit analysis and mapped to relevant compliance standards (e.g., COBIT P09, NIST CSF, ISO 27001).
- Response & Recovery Annexes: Summaries of the BIA, BCP, DRP, and CIRT strategies tailored to the enterprise.
- AI Usage Reflection (2-3 pages): A dedicated appendix explaining "how" and "why" AI was used at various stages (e.g., "We used AI to generate potential attack vectors for our web application, which we then validated against the OWASP Top 10"). It must critically discuss the reliability of the outputs and the team's process for verification.

clos.details: Develop a good understanding of Malware Analysis: today’s greatly increasing malware threats, malware activity mechanism and behavior, malware classification, building an environment to do static and dynamic malware analysis, methods and tools to detect, analyze, reverse-engineer, and eradicate malware.

Identify the different types of Malware Analysis methods: static (ASCII, binary, logical signature detection), dynamic (network traffic analysis, memory forensics, dynamic reverse engineering) and hybrid.

Gain a broad exposure to real world applications of Malware Analysis: take control of the incident, incident response, analyze the threat, examine interactions with the environment, mitigate the risks of malware attempting to escape from the lab,
Set up a relatively inexpensive lab for Malware Analysis activities.
Utilize a standard methodology for detecting, analyzing, reverse engineering, and eradicating malware.
Use a Malware Analysis-based approach in order to resolve real world problems.
Recognize common malware characteristics: propagation, infection, self-defense, capabilities, …
Bypass some of the advanced malware techniques, such as packing, obfuscation and anti-analysis of armored malware breeds.

IAM302.description:
Information Assurance (IA) is a primary example of a field that can benefit greatly from malware analysis. IA aims to protect and defend information and information systems by ensuring their confidentiality, integrity, authentication, availability, and nonrepudiation. This is mostly based on designing measures that would ensure the protection of such systems and their associated data. This makes malware analysis an essential component of IA.
 This course provides students with an effective immersion into the realm of Malware Analysis and Reverse Engineering. It follows a progressive approach that introduces relevant concepts and techniques while preparing students to become effective malware analysts that can use a standard methodology for detecting, analyzing, reverse engineering and eradicating malware.
 Some of the key aspects of this course include reverse engineering malware from various sources and using various programming languages, including Web-based languages such as JavaScript as well as Document-based ones such as VBScript. This is accomplished by using a standard methodology that involves setting up an inexpensive laboratory, isolating it from production environments, and utilizing a selected set of forensic tools in order to dissect the malware, discover its characteristics, and neutralize its effects.
 Scope: The scope of this course includes:
 1. Introduction to Malware Analysis.
 2. Malware Analysis Labs
 3. Methodology to detect, analyze, reverse-engineer, and eradicate malware.
 4. Malware Analysis Applications.
 5. Forensics tools used for Malware Analysis.
 Course Objectives: This course will equip students with the necessary background knowledge in order to become effective Malware Analysis & Reverse Engineering practitioners.

IAP491t.description:
Writing a research thesis is a significant part of academic life. It serves as a comprehensive demonstration of your ability to conduct independent research, contribute to your field of study, and critically engage with existing knowledge. This guide provides a step-by-step approach to help you successfully navigate the research and writing process.
A research thesis is a substantial piece of academic work that presents your research findings, supported by a thorough analysis of relevant literature and data. It is a formal document that follows specific academic standards and demonstrates your ability to:
- Identify a research problem.
- Review and critique existing literature.
- Conduct independent research.
- Analyze and interpret data.
- Present findings clearly and logically.
A research thesis demonstrates your capacity to contribute original knowledge to your field, synthesize existing research, and develop expertise in your chosen topic. It also helps develop critical skills such as analytical thinking, problem-solving, time management, and academic writing.
IAP491t.studentTasks:
(1) Select a project within the chosen IA concentration: Teams should choose a project that aligns with their interests and the scope of the IA concentration. This may involve identifying a real-world problem that can be addressed with IA solutions.
(2) Divide and schedule work: Once the project is chosen, teams should allocate tasks among members based on each individual's strengths and skills. A detailed schedule should be created, outlining milestones and deadlines to ensure timely progress.
(3) Attend all scheduled meetings with supervisor: Teams must commit to regular meetings with their assigned supervisor. These sessions are crucial for receiving guidance, discussing progress, resolving any issues, and making necessary adjustments to the project plan.
(4) Produce document and product according to project requirements: Teams are expected to produce comprehensive documentation and develop the IA product according to the specified requirements. This includes but is not limited to, designing algorithms, coding, testing, and validating the AI model(s). Documentation should detail the problem, methodology, implementation, results, and conclusions.
(5) Present and defend individual contributions in front of the examination board: Each team member must be prepared to present and individually defend their specific contributions to the project in front of the examination board. This includes explaining the rationale behind their approach, the challenges faced, and the solutions implemented.
(6) Students are required to attend at least 80% of scheduled meetings with their supervisor(s) to be eligible for the thesis or capstone defense.

clos.details: Gain an introductory understanding of web security principles and their importance in the context of web applications.
Develop the skills to identify and exploit race conditions, especially related to limit overruns.
Understand the concept of path traversal vulnerabilities and how they can be exploited.
Gain the skills to identify and exploit vulnerabilities related to file uploads.
Understand the concept of information disclosure vulnerabilities and their potential impact on web application security.
Examine vulnerabilities in various authentication mechanisms (password-based and multi-factor authentication).
Learn how to identify, exploit IDOR and Privilege escalation.
Explore vulnerabilities related to OAuth 2.0 authentication mechanisms.
Understand SQL injection vulnerabilities and their exploitation.
Understand OS Command Injection vulnerabilities and their exploitation.
Learn to identify and exploit reflected XSS vulnerabilities.
Understand SSRF vulnerabilities and the potential risks they pose.

IAW301.description: This course provides an immersive learning experience in the field of web application security, featuring the use of PortSwigger as our primary lab material. PortSwigger offers a powerful platform for hands-on exploration of web application vulnerabilities and security best practices. Through this course, students will gain a deep understanding of web application security principles and develop practical skills in a controlled, real-world environment.

clos.details: Describe cultural dimensions based on cultural frameworks and apply them to global business settings.
Develop cultural intelligence to interact and manage people from different cultures.
Developing capability to competently apply course concepts in cross- cultural situations that require responses at the individual, managerial and organisational levels.

Identify the major dimensions of culture relevant to work settings and discuss their effect on behavior in an international environment. Describe negotiation styles in different cultures; adjust negotiation tactics to cultural differences.
Explain the motivation, leadership and HR selection across cultures.
Develop cultural sensitivity needed to succeed in any kind of cross-cultural interactions.
Differentiate the different types of negotiation approaches (integrative, distributive negotiations).
Describe the strategies and actions taken on different stages of negotiations; appreciate and explain the importance of pre-; during and post-negotiation phases.
List the roles and functions in negotiation teams; demonstrate the skills of organizing and managing negotiation teams.
Identify different negotiation scenarios, then formulate and apply the instruments of negotiation strategy and tactics.

IBC201.description:
This course explores the effect of cultural differences on organisational behaviour and negotiation in the global context. It exposes students to issues and problems that inevitably arise in international business when managers have to deal with culturally determined differences in values, attitudes and behaviours. 
The course assists students in developing cross-cultural communication competence and management and negotiation skills to successfully solve problems and capitalise on opportunities in a multicultural environment.

IBI101.description: Introduction to International Business is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles and practices of conducting business in a globalized economy. It explores the dynamic interplay of socio-cultural, economic, technological, and political-legal factors that shape the international business environment. Students will gain insights into the strategies and techniques for entering and operating in foreign markets, including trade policies, global supply chains, and cross-border management. A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications, enabling students to analyze international market trends, optimize decision-making processes, and develop innovative solutions to real-world business challenges. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to navigate the complexities of international business with a forward-thinking, technology-driven approach.

IBS301.description:
This Course is based on the Coursera Specialization "Business Strategy", which covers both the dynamics and the global aspects of strategic management. You'll learn how to evaluate industry evolution, build and sustain competitive advantage, formulate and assess business strategies, and align efforts to organizational strategy. 

The course is divided into two parts. In the first part, you will develop your ability to think strategically, analyze the competitive environment, and recommend firm positioning and value creation. We will explore the underlying theory and frameworks that provide the foundations of a successful business strategy and provide the tools you need to understand that strategy: SWOT, Competitor, Environmental, Five Forces, and Capabilities Analyses, as well as Strategy Maps. 

In the second part, you will advance your strategic analysis skills, by learning the tools to analyze strategy across time (competitive dynamics), industries (corporate strategy), geographies (international strategy), and institutions (non-market strategy). We'll introduce the tools you need to complete a comprehensive evaluation and understand the strategy dynamics of an industry: Competitive Lifecycle, Internationalization and Stakeholder Analyses, and Diversification Matrices.

clos.details: Understand CMOS technology evolution, scaling trends, and the overall VLSI design flow.

Evaluate dynamic behavior of CMOS inverters considering delay, power, and interconnect effects.

ICI211.description: The course is intended to introduce the fundamental concepts of integrated circuit (IC) design, with an emphasis on CMOS-based digital IC design at the introductory level. The course covers the historical development and role of ICs in modern electronic systems; basic NMOS and CMOS integrated circuit technologies; MOS transistor structure and operating principles; static and dynamic behavior of basic CMOS circuits; fundamental performance metrics such as delay, power consumption, noise margin, and area; and the relationship between device characteristics and circuit-level performance. In addition, the course introduces the IC design flow, including logic-level description, transistor-level circuit design, layout concepts, parasitic effects, and basic verification through simulation. Students are exposed to computer-aided design (CAD) tools for circuit modeling and simulation, as well as introductory concepts of testing and design verification.

clos.details: Analyze the international trade environment, trade agreements, market conditions, and product–market–partner information to identify and justify feasible export or import opportunities.
Calculate export prices and import landed costs, prepare commercial quotations, and select and justify appropriate Incoterms® 2020 rules and named places or ports for international transactions.

Draft and evaluate international sales or purchase contracts and selected channel agreements by applying relevant commercial principles, CISG fundamentals, and appropriate allocation of obligations, costs, risks, and remedies.
Design and evaluate transportation, freight-forwarding, cargo-insurance, and claims arrangements appropriate to the goods, route, delivery terms, and transaction risks.
Prepare and audit core export–import documents for accuracy, completeness, and consistency across contract, quotation, shipment, insurance, payment, and customs requirements.

Select and justify international payment, foreign-exchange risk-management, and trade-finance instruments, and identify documentary-credit discrepancies, fraud risks, and appropriate control measures.

Analyze and apply export–import compliance and customs requirements, including trade controls, HS classification, customs valuation, origin, tariffs and taxes, trade remedies, intellectual-property protection, and digital-trade requirements.

Develop, present, and defend an evidence-based, end-to-end export or import transaction project while demonstrating research capability, critical thinking, teamwork, professional communication, ethical judgment, and responsible use of digital and AI tools.

IEI301.description: This course develops the applied knowledge and professional decision-making skills required to plan, execute, control, and evaluate international export–import transactions. The course follows an end-to-end transaction logic covering international trade conditions; product, market, buyer, supplier, and channel research; export pricing and import landed cost; Incoterms® 2020; international sales and channel agreements; transportation, freight forwarding, cargo insurance and claims; trade documents; foreign-exchange exposure; international payment and trade finance; export–import compliance; import regulations; customs entry, HS classification, customs valuation, rules of origin, tariffs and taxes; trade remedies; intellectual-property protection; and digital trade.The course integrates Project-Based Learning and Research-Based Learning through an Integrated Export–Import Transaction Project. Students progressively transform research evidence into a commercially and operationally coherent transaction plan, including costing, quotation, contract, logistics, insurance, payment, compliance, customs, and document-pack outputs. The course emphasizes evidence-based reasoning, cross-document consistency, risk control, ethical conduct, and the ability to present and defend professional decisions.
IEI301.studentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact slots to be eligible for the final examination.- Prepare assigned textbook sections, official references, cases, and worksheets before class.- Participate actively in discussion, calculation workshops, contract and document laboratories, simulations, peer review, and project clinics.- Complete three progress tests, all required individual/in-class tasks, and the Integrated Group Project according to the announced deadlines.- Maintain a traceable record of research evidence, assumptions, calculations, sources, project contributions, and document revisions.- Present and individually defend the group's transaction decisions and submitted evidence in Slots 19–20.- Comply with academic integrity, professional conduct, source-verification, and AI-disclosure requirements.
IEI301.tools: Internet; institutional LMS/FLM/Edunext; presentation software; spreadsheet software; word-processing software; official trade, customs, tariff, logistics, and legal databases; document templates; AI-supported learning tools as directed by the lecturer
IEI301.note: AI Policy: Generative AI and other digital tools may be used only as guided by the lecturer for idea generation, research planning, language refinement, document checking, scenario exploration, and learning support. Students must disclose AI use in assessed coursework, verify outputs against the textbook and authoritative sources, and remain fully responsible for accuracy, legality, originality, confidentiality, and professional judgment. AI use is not permitted in progress tests or the final examination unless explicitly authorized.PBL/RBL evidence and learning products: transaction brief; research evidence matrix; buyer/supplier due-diligence scorecard; channel or sourcing rationale; export-costing/import-landed-cost worksheet; formal quotation or pro forma invoice; Incoterms decision note; draft international sales/purchase contract; logistics and cargo-insurance plan; payment and trade-finance flow; customs and compliance checklist; document pack; risk register; incident-response memorandum; presentation; and individual defence.Central project inquiry: How can an exporter or importer design and execute a commercially viable, documentarily consistent, legally compliant, and risk-controlled international transaction for a selected product, partner, and market?ITU coding used in the Schedule: I = Introduce; T = Teach/Practice; U = Utilize/Integrate.

IFT201c.description:
This Specialization will introduce you to the practice of futures thinking, as developed and applied for the past 50 years by the Institute for the Future, a Silicon-Valley-based research and learning group founded in 1968. You’ll master essential foresight techniques. You’ll meet leading professional futurists. And you’ll choose one or more future topics you want to investigate with your new foresight skills.

The Futures Thinking specialization is for anyone who wants to spot opportunities for innovation and invention faster. You can gain the skills and confidence to help YOU become someone who makes the future, instead of letting the future happen to you. You'll develop a more future-oriented mindset to make positive changes in your own life, as you start to see new possibilities more clearly and craft the personal future you want.

IIP301.description:

It also covers: foreign exchange (forward contracts); documents used in trade; Letter of credit application and instructions; trade terms (Incoterms 2020); Cyber transaction on the Internet. 
Topics mainly include: (1) Key Issues in International Payments. (2) Buyer and the Seller. (3) Basic Terms of Payment (4) Foreign Exchange (5) Various trade terms (Incoterms 2010). (6) Drafts and Acceptances. (7) Documentary Collections. (8) Documentary Credits. (9) Document and Document Checklists. (10) Cyberpayments.

assessments.questionType: Opt.1: Group Project (Case Study Approach)Suggested Topic: Select a real-world case study focused on a company’s marketing communications efforts.Task:- Analyze the company’s existing IMC strategy and tactics, identifying strengths and weaknesses.- Evaluate the effectiveness of the campaign using course frameworks (Strategic Integrated Marketing Communications, Percy & Rosenbaum-Elliott).- Integrate AI tools at multiple stages:++ Secondary Research & Benchmarking – AI-assisted competitor analysis, trend monitoring, market scanning.++ Customer & Audience Insights – AI analytics tools (e.g., Brandwatch, ChatGPT, Google Gemini) for segmentation, persona generation, sentiment analysis.++ Message & Content Testing – AI-generated draft messages, ad copies, or visuals; A/B testing simulations.++ Media Planning – AI scheduling or channel optimization (Buffer AI, Hootsuite, SEMRush, etc.).++ Evaluation & KPIs – AI dashboards to measure engagement, reach, conversion, and sentiment.Opt.2: Group Project (Constructivism Approach)Task: Follow lecturers’ proposal for a guided IMC project.- Students will collaborate under the lecturer’s direction on a selected brand, campaign, or thematic issue.- AI tools will be incorporated into guided exercises at each stage: persona building, content creation, campaign evaluation.
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Duration: 5 WeeksType: Group Project (Max 4–5 members)Deliverables: Written Report + Campaign Proposal + PresentationTask DescriptionStudents will act as an IMC agency team tasked with designing and presenting a fully integrated marketing communication (IMC) campaign for a real brand, product, service, or NGO initiative in the digital environment.The campaign must demonstrate:- Strategic alignment with brand positioning.- Creative integration across communication channels.- Measurable business and communication impact.- Responsible and transparent use of AI tools in research, content creation, execution, and evaluation.Each group may either:- Work with a real client (brand or NGO) and co-develop an IMC campaign.- Choose from a list of provided cases/issues and design a digital-first IMC plan.- Propose a self-selected brand or issue (with instructor approval).- Campaign Proposal Requirements- Executive Summary – overview of campaign concept, objectives, and AI integration highlights.- Situation Analysis – SWOT/PESTLE, competitive benchmarking, and AI-assisted market research (validated by human judgment).- Target Audience & Customer Personas – developed through AI-based analytics (e.g., Brandwatch, ChatGPT, Google Gemini) and refined by team insights.- Campaign Goal & SMART Objectives – clear marketing and communication outcomes.- Key Messages & Storytelling Strategy – alignment with brand voice, adapted for multicultural and digital contexts.- IMC Strategies & Tactics – covering the full spectrum of communication mix, supported by AI tools:++ Advertising (AI-assisted copywriting, visuals, video generation).++ Sales Promotion (AI-powered customer segmentation and targeting).++ Digital/Social Media (AI scheduling, SEO, influencer analysis).++ Public Relations (AI-assisted press kit, sentiment analysis).++ Direct & Interactive Marketing (personalized email/CRM content using AI).++ Creative Samples – mockups, AI-generated content, or prototypes of campaign assets.++ Media & Channel Integration Plan – explain how AI supports message consistency across touchpoints.++ Risk Analysis – potential ethical/privacy issues, AI bias risks, and contingency strategies.++ Budget & Resource Plan – realistic allocation, noting AI tools used for efficiency.++ Evaluation & Metrics – campaign success indicators (engagement, reach, conversion, sentiment, SEO rankings), with AI dashboards for measurement.- Execution Phase (Optional, if feasible)++ May include social media activations, influencer collaborations, digital events, or cross-platform storytelling.AI may be used for asset design, predictive audience targeting, automated scheduling, and real-time performance monitoring—but all outputs must be transparently reported and fact-checked.Deliverables:1. Campaign Proposal Report (max 20 pages):- Situation analysis, objectives, IMC strategies & tactics.- Sample content pieces (with clear AI vs. human contribution).- Integration strategy across platforms.- Campaign evaluation framework.2. Presentation Deck:- Key highlights of campaign strategy, creative outputs, and AI integration.3. Reflection Section (300–500 words per group):- How AI was applied, benefits, limitations, risks, and ethical considerations.
assessments.gradingGuide: According to the predetermined LOs, lecturers have the flexibility to choose assignment forms. Each assignment has a six-day due date, which commences when the lecturers provides detailed instructions. AI is treated as a support tool; human strategic thinking, creativity, and ethical responsibility remain central. All AI-generated outputs must be fact-checked, critically evaluated, and transparently reported. Projects will be graded on: Theoretical application (IMC frameworks), Analytical depth, Creativity, AI integration, Ethical awareness, and Professional presentation. Notes: - Students must show mastery of IMC theories and frameworks (Kliatchko, Percy & Rosenbaum-Elliott, etc.). - AI is a support tool; human creativity, cultural sensitivity, and ethical responsibility remain central. - All AI-generated insights or content must be verified, adapted, and contextualized before use. - Campaigns will be graded on strategic depth, creativity, integration, AI literacy, and professionalism.
assessments.note: Assess the knowledge students have acquired in class up to the time of the assignment.

assessments.questionType: Opt.1: Case Analysis ApproachTask:Conduct a comprehensive analysis of a selected brand’s Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) strategy, applying course theories and AI-supported tools.Students are required to:- Examine messaging consistency across platforms (TV, print, social media, website, influencers, etc.).- Evaluate the IMC approach in terms of:- Target audience segmentation & engagement.- Brand positioning & competitive differentiation.- Alignment with overall marketing objectives.Integrate AI tools at different stages:- Secondary Research: AI-supported competitor benchmarking and trend scanning.- Message Audit: AI clustering of brand messages to detect consistency/inconsistency.- Audience Insight: AI analytics (e.g., Brandwatch, ChatGPT, Gemini) for audience perceptions or sentiment analysis.- Content Testing: AI-assisted drafting of alternative message variations and engagement prediction.Opt.2: Constructivism ApproachTask:Students follow the lecturer’s proposal for an IMC-focused assignment, designed as a step-by-step AI-assisted task.Possible activities include:- Building an AI-generated customer persona for a chosen brand and refining it with human insights.- Producing a short AI-assisted IMC content sample (e.g., social media post, video, infographic) aligned with course theories.- Evaluating a campaign’s AI-powered performance metrics (e.g., reach, sentiment, SEO visibility).
assessments.knowledgeAndSkill: Practice 1 – Buyer Persona & Mini IMC Plan (AI-Supported)Task:Students will be required to create a buyer persona for their most loved brand, applying IMC theories discussed in class and AI-supported tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Brandwatch, audience insight platforms).This practice helps students:- Identify basic IMC concepts (brand positioning, brand-consumer relationship, audience segmentation).- Understand how AI can assist in consumer research and persona creation.- Translate insights into a mini IMC plan (content mission, type, platform).AI Use:- Generate draft personas.- Visualize customer profiles.- Simulate audience responses.Deliverables:- Buyer persona profile (AI-generated draft + human-refined version).- Mini IMC content plan (mission, type, format, platform).- Reflection (300–500 words) on AI use, benefits, risks, and ethical considerations.Practice 2 – AI-Assisted IMC Content CreationTask:Students will develop a media product related to IMC, using AI-powered tools (e.g., Canva AI, Midjourney, Runway for visuals/video; ChatGPT for copywriting; ElevenLabs for voice).Possible outputs:- Social media post.- Short video / podcast snippet.- Infographic.- Interactive digital content.Deliverables:- Final media product (with clear indication of AI vs. human input).- Reflection Report (500–700 words) covering:- AI application process (tools, steps, outcomes).- Benefits & limitations of AI in content creation.- Ethical considerations (bias, copyright, transparency).

They may be asked to submit prompts, and/or AI-generated outputs, and/or a brief reflection explaining how they used the tools and evaluated the outputs.Assignments must explicitly connect to IMC theories and frameworks covered in class (Kliatchko’s IMC, Percy & Rosenbaum-Elliott, brand touchpoints).AI is a supportive tool: students must show where it was used, how it added value, and how they critically evaluated its accuracy and ethics.Submissions will be graded on: Theoretical depth, Analytical rigor, Creativity, AI integration, Ethical awareness, and Report quality.

clos.details: Define and explain the fundamental concepts, terminology, and operational processes in international operations management, including the Input-Transformation-Output model, the process hierarchy, and the 4Vs framework (Volume, Variety, Variation, Visibility).

Analyze the strategic impact of operations decisions on corporate performance across five core performance objectives (Quality, Speed, Dependability, Flexibility, Cost) and evaluate market requirement trade-offs using the Efficient Frontier and Polar Representation.
Evaluate global supply network configurations, offshore/nearshore production strategies, and international facility locations using quantitative tools such as the Weighted-Score Method.

Apply appropriate process designs, manufacturing process types (Project, Batch, Mass, Continuous), and facility layout configurations (Cellular, Product, Functional) to optimize shop-floor material flow and assembly line balancing.

Execute capacity planning, inventory management, and scheduling calculations using operational tools and metrics including Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), ABC Analysis, and Materials Requirements Planning (MRP) logic.

Formulate and propose operations improvement plans by applying Lean manufacturing philosophy (eliminating 7 Wastes/Muda, Value Stream Mapping), Total Quality Management (TQM), risk management, and recovery
Demonstrate the ability to produce a clear, structured academic written report and deliver an effective oral presentation analyzing international manufacturing setup and operational challenges.
Practice effective teamwork, communication, and cross-cultural problem-solving skills to collaboratively design and manage complex global operations projects.

IOM201.description: This course provides a foundation for understanding operations management in a global context. It utilizes the frameworks to analyze how organizations direct, design, deliver, and develop their operations across borders. Specifically, the course covers definitions and concepts of operations management, issues of operations performance, operations strategy, structure and scope of supply, process design and technology, people in operations, planning and control, capacity management, inventory management, operations improvement, lean operations, quality management, risk management, and recovery.

Final Result = OGA*50% + TDA*50%
In which:
1) On-going Assessment (OGA)
 - Project Introduction (Report 1): 4%
 - Project Management Plan (Report 2): 8%
 - System Requirement (Report 3): 16%
 - System Design (Report 4): 18%
 - Testing (Report 5): 18%
 - User Guides (Report 6): 4%
 - Implementation (Report 7): 32%
2) Thesis Defense Assessment (TDA)
 - Project Introduction: 5%
 - Project Management Plan: 5%
 - System Requirement: 15%
 - System Design: 10%
 - Testing: 10%
 - User Guides: 5%
 - Implementation: 35% 
 - Presentation Skills: 5%

Completion Criteria: 
1. OGA >= 5
2. TDA >= 4/10

Before thesis defense, students must wait until the second thesis defense round if they have the OGA less than 5/10 OR they are in one of below cases:
(1) Students can't prove the fact that they prepare any of the project reports or the output system by themselves
(2) There are more than 3 obvious logic defects OR more than 1 show-stopper defects (the defects that prevent end user from completing his/her use case on any system functions) in the submitted system.

The student(s) has to re-do the capstone project if the above cases occur with the assessments for the second thesis defense OR there is one OGA with grade (see the list above) less than 2/10.

After thesis defense, student(s) is evaluated as failed the capstone project if they are in one of below cases (no matter when the guiding teacher doesn't evaluate that):
(1) Student can't demonstrate any function or use case
(2) Students can't prove the fact that they prepare any of the project reports or the output system by themselves
(3) There are more than 3 obvious logic defects OR more than 1 show-stopper defects (the defects that prevent end user from completing his/her use case on any system functions) in the submitted system.

IOS301.description:
This course is designed based on the course of IoT Fundamentals: IoT Security (Cisco).
The advent of the Internet of Things (IoT) has created many new opportunities for connecting people, places, and things. It has also brought with it an ever-expanding attack surface for threat actors to exploit. Today's organizations are challenged with securely implementing many new devices into the existing information technology (IT) infrastructure. The IoT Security course arms students with crucial knowledge they need to intelligently discuss and evaluate, at a basic level, the IoT security environment for a given business context.

IPD201.description: The first part of this course provides: the theory related to the function of pictograms; the methodology to create a pictogram then a family of icons; and the ability to plan a project from concept development to applying icons across different media. The second part focuses on learning how to design a pattern by understanding its anatomy and experimenting with various design techniques. Methodologies for creating patterns are explored through research and creative exploration. Throughout the course, students are encouraged to explore emerging AI tools as optional supportive resources—such as using AI to generate visual references, simulate form variations, or test icon applications across different platforms. Students must ensure that AI use does not replace core design processes like conceptual sketching, structural planning, or creative decision-making. Any use of AI must be clearly documented with the tool’s name, purpose, and stage of use in accompanying reports or project notes. The course provides knowledge about the history of development, the role, and the application of pictograms in graphic design. It offers techniques for designing individual icons and icon systems, along with skills for managing and applying icon systems across multiple platforms. It provides knowledge about the development and application of patterns at each stage, including current design trends and usage in modern graphic design. It offers a structured approach to researching, shaping, and developing patterns. It provides techniques for the flexible application of patterns on different objects and formats. Additionally, students may enhance their final presentations through AI-assisted visualizations or animation mockups, as long as they are supplementary and not substitutes for the hand-designed core deliverables.

IPD201.note: Do not use AI to fully replace design thinking or hand-drawing. Final products must reflect individual thinking processes and demonstrate form-making skills. Clearly cite any AI tools used in the report, including the tool’s name, its role, and the stage in which it was applied. Do not submit works entirely generated by AI, such as icons, patterns, or animations, without accompanying sketches and original work created by the student. AI is encouraged to be used in a supporting role only—for example, to search for reference materials, simulate models for study, or enhance visual presentation. Students may receive point deductions or be rated poorly if: They are dishonest in reporting AI usage; They copy ideas from AI tools without further developing or personalizing them; They overuse AI to cover up a lack of personal creative investment.

IPR102.description:
This course provides fundamental concepts, principles, and rules concerning different types of intellectual property rights relating to graphic design and/or multimedia communication, particularly copyright, trademark, and registered design.
Students will learn how to apply these principles and rules to protect their intellectual property rights in relation to their graphic design works and/or multimedia communication work.
During the course, there are several typical cases regarding intellectual property rights relevant to graphic designs and/or multimedia communication available for students to analyze and discuss.
Students are also provided with basic skills such as how to acquire intellectual property protection for their creative products, how to avoid infringing on other people's intellectual property rights when creating new works, and how to commercialize their intellectual property rights.
In addition to common teaching methods such as lectures, brainstorming, and group discussion, the instructor will also use teaching methods specific to law, such as case studies, problem-solving, and moot court exercises.

materials.author: Kenneth C. LaudonJane P. Laudon

clos.details: Explain the foundational concepts of information systems, including their definition, core components (management – organization – technology), the role of IS in digital enterprises, and the relationship between IS and business processes

Analyze the components of modern IT infrastructure, including cloud computing, mobile platforms, data storage and database management systems, computer networks, and emerging technologies such as IoT, AI, and data analytics
Apply knowledge of enterprise systems (ERP, SCM, CRM) and e-commerce systems to analyze how organizations achieve operational excellence and competitive advantage in a digital environment

Evaluate information strategies and digital business models using analytical frameworks such as Porter's Five Forces, the Value Chain Model, and global IS architecture, in order to propose IS solutions aligned with organizational objectives

Model and analyze business processes, identify business process redesign (BPR) opportunities enabled by IS, and select appropriate system development methodologies (SDLC, Agile, RAD, Prototyping) for given organizational contexts

Work with relational databases, Business Intelligence tools, and fundamental data analytics techniques (OLAP, data mining, dashboards) to support decision-making across different management levels within an organization

Identify and analyze information security risks, ethical, social, and legal issues in IS use (privacy, intellectual property, legal liability), and propose appropriate security controls and governance policies

Articulate the principles of IS project management, assess system implementation risks, and analyze the unique challenges of building and operating information systems in the context of global business organizations

ISD201.description: This course provides an overview of how information systems support business operations, decision-making, and digital transformation in modern organizations. Students will explore core topics such as business processes, enterprise systems, databases, networks, cybersecurity, e-commerce, knowledge management and artificial intelligence. The course emphasizes how organizations use information systems strategically to achieve operational excellence, improve decision-making, and gain competitive advantage, so that learners know how information systems are transforming global business, and why they are so essential for running and managing a business today. Through real-world case studies and practical activities, students will analyze the structure of digital firms, model business processes, and evaluate system solutions. Key technologies such as cloud computing, data analytics, and business intelligence are introduced. Ethical and social issues related to data and systems use are also discussed. The course bridges business needs with IT capabilities, equipping students with foundational knowledge to work at the intersection of business and technology.

clos.details: Describe the concept of ERP and the ERP model
Explain how ERP is used to integrate business processes
Setup an open source ERP system and implement one main module (M/S, SCM, A/F, H/R)
Describe the elements of a value chain, and explain how core processes relate
Identify the international issues that impact a worldwide implementation of ERP
Explain how the key elements of organizational change management apply to an ERP implementation

ISM302.description:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
 * Describe the concept of ERP and the ERP model; define key terms; explain the transition from MRP to ERP; identify the levels of ERP maturity.
 * Explain how ERP is used to integrate business processes; define and analyze a process; create a process map and improve and/or simplify the process; apply the result to an ERP implementation.
 * Setup an open source ERP system and implement one main module (M/S, SCM, A/F, H/R)
 * Describe the elements of a value chain, and explain how core processes relate; identify how the organizational infrastructure supports core business processes; explain the effect of a new product launch on the three core business processes.
 * Identify the international issues that impact a worldwide implementation of ERP; identify the key technological considerations and infrastructure concerns in ERP implementation; describe the strategic use of technology for ERP.
 * Explain how the key elements of organizational change management apply to an ERP implementation; define change readiness; describe a learning requirements plan; explain the use of assessment tools to identify the readiness of an organization to change; identify the methods of implementing and sustaining the change.
 * Describe project organizational considerations; define the project management tools and resources needed to implement an ERP system; describe the roles and responsibilities of the key organization players; describe the tactics, tools, and methodologies available to implement ERP; evaluate the success of the implementation.
 * Describe how the knowledge management capability of an ERP system can be used to sustain competitive advantage; describe how to use ERP to communicate effectively with customers and suppliers.

ISP391.description:
The course is designed as a project-based learning course where students could apply fully-equipped knowledges to design simple real systems based on KITs from manufacturers such as Free Scales, Nouvoton and Phoenix. Students can select one of seven different projects for students to practice in team. Names of projects:
1. Monitoring and controlling room temperature based on ARM Freescale
2. Monitoring and controlling room temperature based on ARM Nuvoton
3.Monitoring and controlling room temperature based on PLC
4. Main Controller for Smarthome based on ARM.
5. Game Controller based on ARM.
6. Traffic light Controller based on PLC.
7. Home weather station based on ARM
A programmable logic controller (PLC) is an electronic device used in many industries to monitor and control building systems and production processes. Unlike PCs and smartphones, which are designed to perform any number of roles, a PLC is designed to perform a single set of tasks, except under real-time constraints and with superior reliability and performance.
To meet the demands of harsh industrial environments, PLCs are designed to be extremely robust, often capable of withstanding extreme temperatures, humidity, vibration, and electrical noise. Logic controllers are commonly tasked with monitoring and controlling a very large number of sensors and actuators, and are therefore distinct from other computer systems in their extensive input/output (I/O) arrangements.
The ARM Cortex-M is a group of 32-bit RISC ARM processor cores licensed by ARM Holdings. The cores are intended for microcontroller use, and consist of the Cortex-M0, M0+, M1, M3, M4, and M7. ARM core processors can support powerful peripherals and connectivity

assessments.duration: ~ 30 minutes for presentation, ~ 60 minutes for demo and Q&A. Total is 90 minutes.
assessments.gradingGuide: Thesis Defense Assessment (TDA): - Project Introduction: 5% - Project Management Plan: 5% - Software Requirement: 15% - Software Design: 10% - Testing: 10% - User Guides: 5% - Implementation: 35% - Presentation Skills: 5% - Q&A: 10% Presentation mark is given by each member of defence committee for each student on final project presentation. Personal mark is the average of all marks given by members of defence committee.
assessments.note:
One or more specific members of the student team is not allowed to join the thesis defense (and therefore being failed the subject) if he/she has OGA less than 5 or any cheating found from him/her (he/she can't prove they do the software product by him/herself).

Before thesis defense, the student team must wait until the second round of thesis defense if the whole team has the OGA less than 5/10 OR they are in one of below cases:
(1) The team completes less than 75% use cases functions/screens as submitted (as mentioned in the submitted Report 3, at the end of the week 3) OR there are less than 20 average (3-7 transactions) use cases completed.
(2) The team can't prove the fact that they prepare any of the project reports or the output software package by themselves
(3) There are more than 3 obvious coding-logic defects OR more than 1 show-stopper defects (the defects that prevent end user from completing his/her use case on any software functions) in the submitted software.

The student(s) has to re-do the capstone project if the above cases occur with the assessments for the second thesis defense OR there is one OGA with grade less than 2/10.

After thesis defense, one or more team members are evaluated as failed the capstone project if they are in one of below cases (no matter when the guiding teacher doesn't evaluate that):
(1) Student can't demonstrate any function or use case
(2) Students can't prove the fact that they prepare any of the project reports or the output software by themselves
(3) There are more than 3 obvious coding-logic defects OR more than 1 show-stopper defects (the defects that prevent end user from completing his/her use case on any software functions) in the submitted software.

ISP490.description:
The capstone project provides students important skills and initial experiences in participating in the software projects. Student can apply knowledges they have learned to the real current projects include:
- Experiencing across all project phases: requirement, design, coding, testing and release
- Finding out and using the templates and composing documents for each project stage
- Using knowledges of technology that have been taught
- Having the opportunity to research and apply new technologies
- Practicing teamwork and how to interact with colleagues in a project implementation process
- Ensuring the proper implementation of quality requirements and schedule
- Doing troubleshooting

With the team size of 4-5 members, the output product size are required to be equivalent to 20-25 medium use cases (3-7 transactions for each use case; action buttons on the screen, end user interactions to the software screens/functions or database transactions can be counted as transaction). In cases where the number of students is insufficient to form groups, the campus may adjust the number of students to suit the actual training conditions.

The capstone project provides students, working in groups, with a significant project experience in which they can integrate much of the material they have learned in their program, including matters relating to requirements, design, implementation, human factors, professionalism, and project management. Students should be expected to deliver one or several iterations of a software system, along with all artifacts appropriate to the process model they are using. These would likely include 
a) Project management Plan (perhaps updated regularly), 
b) Software Requirements Specifications (SRS)
c) Software Design Documents (SDD)
d) Test Plan and other Test Documentation (STD)
e) Software package & the user guides (package content, installation guide & user manuals)

All the documents in the project implementation process and the progress reports are required to write in English.

ITE302c.description: Organizations and governments are seeking out ethics professionals to minimize risk and guide their decision-making about the design of inclusive, responsible, and trusted technology. An algorithm not designed and assessed in alignment with ethical standards can create further inequity across race, gender and marginalized populations. The reputational and financial impact of an ethics violation can devastate a company. clos.details: Nắm được lí thuyết cơ bản về phiên dịch, hiểu và rèn luyện được các kĩ năng cơ bản của quá trình phiên dịch như nghe hiểu, giữ nhớ, diễn đạt lại.
Rèn luyện kĩ năng nghe hiểu nhanh, chính xác.
Rèn luyện kĩ năng giữ nhớ (khả năng ghi nhớ, ghi chép và tóm tắt nội dung).
Rèn luyện kĩ năng shadowing.
Rèn luyện kĩ năng diễn đạt lại (dịch chuyển đổi số từ, cách hô-gọi trong chào hỏi xã giao, các câu chào hỏi, giới thiệu trong các ngữ cảnh).
Rèn luyện kĩ năng dịch có văn bản sight translation.
Rèn luyện kĩ năng dịch trong trường hợp phỏng vấn cơ bản.
Rèn luyện kĩ năng đánh giá, rà soát bản dịch của bản thân.
Rèn luyện kĩ năng dịch nhanh, chính xác, đúng ngữ cảnh.
Rèn luyện tác phong của người phiên dịch viên.

JBI301.description:
II. Mục tiêu của môn học: 
 (1) Cung cấp các kiến thức cơ sở, cơ bản về các loại hình, các quá trình của việc phiên dịch tiếng Nhật-Việt, Việt-Nhật.
 (2) Giúp sinh viên nắm được các kiến thức, kĩ năng cần có trong quá trình phiên dịch.
 (3) Giúp sinh viên rèn luyện các kĩ năng cơ bản như nghe hiểu, giữ nhớ, diễn đạt lại, tìm ra phương án dịch chính xác, nhanh chóng.
 (4) Giúp sinh viên rèn luyện và trau dồi khả năng dịch thuật trong những lĩnh vực cơ bản.
 (5) Giúp sinh viên có khả năng nghe và đánh giá các video liên quan đến dịch nói.

III. Hình thức triển khai môn học: xem cụ thể các nội dung trong Grading structure
Môn học kéo dài trong 10 tuần, mỗi tuần 2 slots, được tiến hành theo hình thức kết hợp giờ học trên lớp và bài tập tại nhà. Cụ thể như sau:
+Giáo viên trình bày các nội dung lí thuyết, các kĩ năng cần có trong phiên dịch thông qua slide trên lớp.
+Giao bài tập thực hành ngắn trên lớp, giáo viên gọi từng sinh viên thực hành dịch đoạn CD có sẵn hoặc câu do giáo viên nói. Cho sinh viên luyện dịch theo cặp và giáo viên nhận xét, chỉnh sửa.
+Bài tập về nhà: giao file, yêu cầu nghe, viết lại script và dịch theo nhóm hoặc cá nhân và gửi lại cho giáo viên trước giờ lên lớp.

- Tham dự tối thiểu 80% số giờ học trên lớp mới đủ điều kiện tham gia thi kì thi cuối môn.

- Làm bài tập về nhà theo yêu cầu của giảng viên.
- Tích cực nghe và luyện tập để nâng cao năng lực của bản thân.
