clos.details: Analyze the role, organizational structure, and functions of the housekeeping department within hotels, and identify modern operational trends in the hospitality industry.
Apply standardized procedures for inspecting and servicing guest rooms, public areas, and specialized equipment to ensure service quality and safety.
Assess and monitor specifications for supplies, chemicals, and equipment used in housekeeping, in compliance with safety regulations and cost-control practices.
Operate and supervise maintenance tasks, laundry services, inventory distribution, guest guidance, ensuring hotel standards and occupational safety.
Manage human resources in the housekeeping department: planning staff allocation, training programs, performance evaluation, and promoting teamwork and discipline.
Analyze principles of cost control, manage consumables inventory, establish stock auditing procedures, and prepare periodic housekeeping cost reports.
Propose methods to enhance service quality, develop processes for handling guest complaints, and practice effective and professional communication in a multicultural hotel environment.
Plan, organize, and coordinate the provision of additional services (flowers, beverages, gifts, decorations) to meet special guest requirements for events and small functions in the hotel.
Demonstrate problem-solving skills for operational incidents (safety, emergencies, property loss, operational risks) encountered in housekeeping operations.
Commit to professional standards, uphold a positive and responsible attitude, and demonstrate environmental and occupational safety awareness in all professional activities.

Main objective: This course equips students with comprehensive foundation and specialized knowledge of hotel housekeeping operations. Learners will develop skills in managing resources, controlling costs and human resources, delivering quality service, problem-solving and responding to operational incidents, applying professional standards and fostering environmental awareness, to meet the demands of modern hospitality management.
-Description: Housekeeping Operations explores core and advanced functions of the hotel housekeeping department, including cleaning and inspection procedures for guest rooms and public areas, inventory and equipment management, cost control, human resource management, laundry and maintenance supervision, service quality enhancement, guest complaint handling, and special event support. The course emphasizes teamwork, discipline, professional attitude, and effective communication for multicultural settings.
-Teaching method: The course applies diverse pedagogical approaches such as lectures, analytical discussions, skills demonstrations, collaborative group work, roleplay, case studies, problem-based learning, and project planning for service scenarios. Assessment is integrated through applied exercises, situational analysis, and teamwork performance.

clos.details: Analyze the role, organization, and professional standards of the housekeeping department within different types of lodging establishments; explain how housekeeping interacts with other divisions to optimize guest experience.

Evaluate and apply advanced management concepts relevant to executive housekeeping, including planning, organizing, directing, coordinating, and controlling resources to achieve departmental and organizational goals.
Effectively implement inventory management, cost control, and budgetary practices in housekeeping operations, ensuring efficient utilization of equipment, supplies, and labor.
Demonstrate knowledge and skills in managing technical operations: cleaning procedures, laundry, floor care, and preventive maintenance in compliance with quality standards and safety regulations.
Manage human resources in the housekeeping department: from recruiting, training, motivating, evaluating, to fostering an inclusive and productive work environment.
Analyze and respond to emerging risks related to safety, security, infectious diseases, and implement sustainable environmental management practices in lodging properties.
Develop effective communication, team leadership, and problem-solving skills to address operational challenges, guest complaints, and multicultural workforce dynamics in the housekeeping department.

Demonstrate professional ethics, responsibility, and adaptability in decision-making as an executive housekeeper; contribute to the sustainable development and competitive advantage of the hospitality organization.

LOD214.description:
Main objective: This course is designed to develop advanced knowledge, managerial thinking, and professional competencies essential for executive housekeepers in hotel and lodging establishments. Students will acquire expertise in departmental organization, asset and inventory management, human resources, quality assurance, risk and environmental management, and the integration of professional ethics and sustainable practices to enhance both operational efficiency and guest satisfaction.
-Description: Through a comprehensive structure reflecting current industry standards, the course explores the strategic and technical responsibilities of executive housekeepers, including department planning; organizing, directing, and controlling resources; budget and labor control; equipment, laundry, and cleaning operations; as well as health, safety, and environmental leadership. Emphasis is placed on human resource management, communication and teamwork in multicultural environments, problem-solving, total quality management (TQM), and effective interaction with other hotel divisions to achieve organizational goals. Case studies, practical issues (from the textbook), and real-world scenarios are incorporated to strengthen the link between theory and practice, while fostering ethics and adaptability in decision-making.
-Teaching method: A blend of teaching strategies is adopted, including interactive lectures, case study analysis, group discussion, skill demonstration, management simulation, situational problem-solving, collaborative projects, and hands-on practice drawn from the textbook’s minicases and operational cases. Students are assessed through a variety of methods—applied exercises, quizzes, group/individual assignments, scenario analyses, and projects—focusing on both knowledge integration and the application of managerial and technical skills to real and simulated housekeeping challenges.
-Completion Criteria:
Every on-going assessment component > 0; Final Result >=5 & Final Exam Score >= 4

clos.details: Explain the architecture and components of an Embedded Linux system, including the bootloader, Linux kernel, root filesystem, and hardware abstraction layers.
Configure and use cross-compilation toolchains and development environments to build software for embedded target platforms.
Build, configure, and deploy a customized Embedded Linux system, including kernel configuration, root filesystem creation, and boot process management.
Develop embedded Linux applications using system programming techniques such as file I/O, process management, threading, and inter-process communication.
Apply debugging and performance analysis tools (e.g., GDB, strace, profiling tools) to identify and resolve software issues in Embedded Linux systems.
Design and implement a complete Embedded Linux solution for a target device, integrating system configuration, application development, and testing.

LOS201.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and development techniques of Embedded Linux systems. Students learn how to build and configure Linux-based embedded platforms, including cross-compilation toolchains, bootloaders, the Linux kernel, and root file systems. The course also covers system programming concepts, device driver basics, and embedded system debugging techniques. Through hands-on labs and assignments, students gain practical experience in building and deploying custom Embedded Linux systems for embedded devices.

Biết được các đặc trưng về cấu trúc ngôn ngữ: Tính tuyến tính của ngôn ngữ và tính quy tắc trong sắp xếp các yếu tố trong câu. Nắm được lí thuyết liên quan đến hình vị học, các loại hình vị và chức năng của hình vị trong ngôn ngữ, các kiến thức liên quan đến ngữ nghĩa học ở các cấp độ khác nhau như: từ, cụm từ hay câu.
Hiểu được ý nghĩa của Ngữ dụng học và các tiên đề liên quan đến ngữ dụng học. Ngữ pháp học.
Nắm được các kiến thức liên quan đến Ngôn ngữ học: mối tương quan về mặt xã hội, ngữ cảnh, nhận thức, các quy luật về âm vị học và các loại hình của ngôn ngữ.

Tăng cường trải nghiệm nghiên cứu và trình bày kết quả nghiên cứu qua những nội dung quan tâm liên quan đến ngôn ngữ học. Tăng cường khả năng làm việc nhóm, phối hợp để cùng làm việc qua các hoạt động để tạo ra các LO ở trên

LTG203.description:
I. Yêu cầu định hướng triển khai của môn học: 
Môn học thuộc học phần Kiến thức - Kỹ năng ngôn ngữ, được cung cấp cho sinh viên sau khi hoàn thành các kiến thức kỹ năng tiếng, góp phần xây dựng kiến thức cơ sở, cơ bản về lí luận ngôn ngữ của Ngành. 
II. Mục tiêu của môn học: 
 (1) Góp phần củng cố kiến thức thực hành tiếng, giúp sinh viên hiểu được bản chất của ngôn ngữ nói chung và ngôn ngữ Nhật qua việc lồng ghép các thí dụ cụ thể trong phần thực hành tiếng và huy động các kiến thức về tiếng Việt, tiếng Anh mà sinh viên đã biết ở các mức độ khác nhau trước đó. Đưa các kiến thức thực hành tiếng này vào trong nhận thức lí thuyết của ngành học. 
(2) Cung cấp cho sinh viên các kiến thức Lý thuyết nhập môn về ngành Ngôn ngữ học: Tính đồng đại và tính phổ quát của ngôn ngữ. 
(3) Trang bị cho sinh viên kiến thức cơ sở về mối quan hệ giữa các từ vựng, giữa các cụm từ vũng như mối quan hệ giữa các câu trong ngôn ngữ. Từ đó sinh viên có thể thấy được đặc trưng của ngôn ngữ nhìn từ góc độ 1 từ, 1 cụm từ hay 1 câu văn đầy đủ.
LTG203.studentTasks:
- Sinh viên đọc tài liệu nghiên cứu bằng tiếng Việt và trình bày lại cách hiểu về các nội dung được giao đọc (bằng tiếng Việt) theo các nhóm. Việc này nhằm giúp sinh viên nắm được kiến thức chuyên môn của môn học bằng tiếng mẹ đẻ trước khi tiếp xúc với bài giảng bằng tiếng Nhật.
- Sinh viên tập nghiên cứu các vấn đề về tiếng Nhật hoặc tiếng Việt hoặc so sánh đối chiếu 2 ngôn ngữ Nhật - Việt. Các vấn đề này có liên quan đến nội dung môn học hoặc do sinh viên quan tâm và muốn tìm hiểu thêm.
- Sinh viên dùng AI chuẩn bị bài và làm bài trước khi lên lớp.
- Sinh viên tham gia đầy đủ giờ học để đảm bảo thu nhận đầy đủ kiến thức, tham gia tối thiểu 80% thời lượng khóa học mới đủ điều kiện thi cuối kì.

materials.description: Ngữ âm: 毎日練習!リズムで身につく日本語の発音 (Phát âm tiếng Nhật - Luyện tập bằng nhịp điệu)
Từ vựng: 日本語教育能力検定試験に合格するための語彙 (Từ vựng để thi đỗ kỳ thi sát hạch năng lực giảng dạy tiếng Nhật)
Ngữ pháp: 日本人のための日本語文法入門 (Nhập môn Ngữ pháp tiếng Nhật dành cho người Nhật)
1) 基礎日本語文法 (Ngữ pháp tiếng Nhật cơ sở)
2) にほんご音読トレーニング (Luyện đọc âm tiếng Nhật)
3) 日本語の発音教室―理論と練習 (Lớp học phát âm tiếng Nhật - Lý thuyết và thực hành)
4) 日本語アクセント辞典 (Từ điển ngữ âm tiếng Nhật)

clos.details: LO1: Nắm được về căn bản những kiến thức về ngữ âm trong tiếng Nhật (cấu tạo âm, phách, nhịp)
LO2: Nắm được kiến thức nền và luyện tập để sửa và hoàn thiện cách phát âm các loại âm trong tiếng Nhật
LO3: Hiểu về cơ bản những khái niệm về cách lên xuống giọng, cách ngắt giữa các từ, nhấn mạnh và thực hành được
L04: Nắm được những thông tin căn bản cấu trúc ngữ pháp trong tiếng Nhật, đọc và hiểu được những từ chuyên môn tiếng Nhật trong lĩnh vực này
LO5: Hiểu khái quát về từ vựng trong ngôn ngữ nói chung và tiếng Nhật nói riêng (hệ thống từ vựng, số lượng từ vựng, loại hình từ vựng...)
LO6: Nâng cao được vốn từ, chữ Hán và ngữ pháp ở mức độ trung cấp

LTJ301.description:
Nội dung học bao gồm:
1) Phần 1: Ngữ pháp tiếng Nhật hiện đại
- Cấu trúc Ngữ pháp tiếng Nhật
- Khái quát về Thời, Thể
- Về tha động từ, tự động từ
- Cấu trúc câu phức
2) Phần 2: Từ vựng trong tiếng Nhật
- Cấu tạo từ
- Ý nghĩa từ
- Từ ghép, liên từ...
- Từ tượng thanh & Từ tượng hình
3) Phần 3: Ngữ âm và phát âm
- Nhịp, phách trong tiếng Nhật
- Luyện phát âm (âm dài, âm ngắt, âm ghép)
- Cách kiểu lên xuống trong tiếng Nhật
LTJ301.studentTasks:
Để giờ học diễn ra hiệu quả, sinh viên cần:
- sinh viên tham gia học > 80% thời lượng khóa học mới đủ điều kiện thi cuối kì
- đọc trước tài liệu, tra từ, hiểu từ để có khái niệm cơ bản
- trên lớp tích cực tham gia trao đổi, thảo luận về chủ đề được đưa ra
- thực hiện đầy đủ các yêu cầu của giảng viên về thực hành, bài tập, báo cáo, thu hoạch (nếu có) và nộp đúng thời hạn
- sử dụng laptop phục vụ múc đích tìm hiểu, nghiên cứu
- thường xuyên truy cập trang cms.fpt.edu.vn để cập nhật tài liệu, yêu cầu của giảng viên

Điểm điều kiện áp dụng với tất cả sinh viên theo học chương trình tiếng Anh chuẩn bị tại LUK Global. Đây là điều kiện để sinh viên hoàn thành từng cấp độ học.

Các trường hợp vi phạm điểm điều kiện:
- Vi phạm ngôn ngữ sử dụng tại LUK Global [Ngôn ngữ tại LUK Global là 100% tiếng Anh]
Lần 1: Cảnh cáo
Lần 2: Trừ 3 điểm điều kiện
Lần 3: Ghi điểm điều kiện = 0 điểm

- Gian lận điểm danh
Sinh viên đi học hộ hoặc nhờ người đi học hộ: Ghi điểm điều kiện = 0 điểm
Sinh viên điểm danh vân tay nhưng không tham gia giờ học: Ghi điểm điều kiện = 0 điểm

- Sinh viên không tham gia học tiếp sau giờ social time:
Lần 1: Cảnh cáo

clos.details:
Manipulate logical expressions and use logic for inference 
LO1.1 Determine the truth value of a proposition; check if two propositions are equivalent; translate between logical expressions and sentences for propositional logic.
LO1.2 Determine the truth value of a proposition; check if two propositions are equivalent; translate between logical expressions and sentences for predicate logic. 
LO1.3 Manipulate logical expressions with nested quantifiers.
LO1.4 Recognize the inference rules used in a valid statemment; use inference rules to draw conclusions; check if a statement is valid.

Perform basic operations on sets, functions and sequences 
LO2.1 Distinguish basic terminologies in set theory; find the power set and cartersian product; represent a subset using binary bits.
LO2.2 Perform operations on sets; check if two sets are equal.
LO2.3 Determine if a given rule represents a function; perform operations on functions and manipulate functions inlvolving the floor and the ceiling functions. 
LO2.4 Determine if a function is one-to-one, onto or a bijection, and describe how these properties can be used to compare two sets.
LO2.5 Find a formula for a sequence; evaluate a finite sum with a possible use of special summations.

Analyze basic algorithms written in pseudo codes and determine their complexities 
LO3.1 Determine if a procedure is an algorithm; work out basic algorithms written in pseudocodes including searching, sorting and greedy algorithms.
LO3.2 Find big-O, big-Omega and big-Theta estimates of a function; describe complexity of an algorithm.

Discuss applications of modular arithmetic and analyze algorithms on integers 
LO4.1 Perform integer division and modular arithmetic; apply congruence in generating pseudorandom numbers and in cryptology. 
LO4.2 Find the base b expansion of an integer; perform binary operations and modular exponentiation on integers. 
LO4.3 Check if a number is prime and find prime factorization of an integer; find greatest common divisor and least common multiple.

Use induction and recursive definition to prove a statement or to describe an object, and write recursive algorithms 
LO5.1 Prove mathematical statements by induction. 
LO5.2 Manipulate sequences and sets defined by recursion. 
LO5.3 Work out recursive algorithms, including the mergesort algorithm; distinguish between iterative and recursive algorithms.

Solve counting problems 
LO6.1 Use basic rules for counting
LO6.2 Use recurrence relations for counting, including divide-and-conquer recurrence relations.

Analyze the structure of a graph and find shortest paths in a weighted graph 
LO7.1 Classify and describe a graph; use hand-shaking theorem to analyze a graph; identify special graphs including bipartite graphs.
LO7.2 Represent a graph using incidence and adjacency matrices; determine if two graphs are isomorphic.
LO7.3 Check connectivity of a graph and identify its connected components; count paths in a graph.
LO7.4 Determine if a graph has Euler/Hamilton paths/circuits; find Euler and Hamilton paths/circuits in a graph. 
LO7.5 Run Dijsktra's algorithm to determine the shortest paths and the shortest distance in a weighted graph.

Analyze the structure of a tree and describe algorithms using trees 
LO8.1 Check if a graph is a tree, and identify basic terminologies of a tree; use properties of m-ary trees to solve problems.
LO8.2 Build binary search trees and decision trees; analyze complexities of algorithms described using binary search trees and decision trees.
LO8.3 Recognize and construct prefix codes; build optimal trees using Huffman coding.
LO8.4 Traverse a tree and use tree traversal to generate notations; evaluate prefix and postfix expressions.
LO8.5 Run Depth-first search and Breadth-first search algorithms to find spanning trees 
LO8.6 Find minimum spanning trees using Prim, Kruskal,... algorithms

clos.details:
Describe basic properties and find the limit of a function
LO1.1 Find the domain, range, zeros and analyze the symmetry of the graph; create new functions from old functions.
LO1.2 Find the slope and write an equation of a line; describe how a function changes under graph translations.
LO1.3 Compute the limit of a function using graphs and limit laws, including the Squeeze's Theorem.
LO1.4 Find limits at infinity and infinity limits, and apply in finding asymptotes of a function.
LO1.5 Identify where a function is continuous; use the Intermedia Value Theorem to show that an equation has a solution.

Calculate derivatives of a function
LO2.1 Find the average rate of change; identify derivative as the limit of a difference quotient. 
LO2.2 Recognize derivative as the instantaneous velocity and the slope of tangent lines.
LO2.3 Find derivatives using basic formulas and the sum, difference, product, quotient, chain rules.

Use derivatives to analyze a function and to solve applications
LO3.1 Use implicit differentiation to find derivatives and to solve related rates problems.
LO3.2 Find linear approximation of a function; calculate differentials and apply in calculating errors of approximation.
LO3.3 Apply Rolle's Theorem and Mean Value Theorem to a function; find critical numbers and absolute extrema of a function. 
LO3.4 Identify local extrema, and describe the monotonicity of a function; solve optimization problems.
LO3.5 Recognize acceleration as second derivative; determine inflection points and describe the concavity of a function.
LO3.6 Use Newton method to approximate solutions of an equation.

Calculate integrals and find area under the graph of a function
LO4.1 Use Riemann sums to approximate area; recognize area as a definite integral which is the limit of Riemann sums.
LO4.2 Apply the Fundamental Theorems of Calculus to find derivatives of integrals, and to evaluate definite integrals. 
LO4.3 Recognize indefinite integrals as anti-derivatives; find integrals using basic formulas and the techniques of substitution and integration by parts.
LO4.4 Use integration to solve applications and to compute the average value of a function. 
LO4.5 Approximate definite integrals using Midpoint, Trapezoidal and Simpson rules. 
LO4.6 Determine if an improper integral converges.

Solve a system of linear equations using Gaussian elimination
LO5.1 Identify if a matrix is in echelon forms; carry a matrix into an echelon using row operations; calculate the rank of a matrix. 
LO5.2 Use echelon matrices to solve/describe the solution set of a linear system.

Perform basic operations on matrices and manipulate matrix transformations
LO6.1 Perform addition, scalar multiplication and transpose of matrices; verify if a matrix is symmetric.
LO6.2 Multiply two matrices of appropriate sizes; transform between a linear system and a matrix equation.
LO6.3 Determine the matrix of a linear transformation; use properties of linear transformations in solving problems.

Find the determinant, inverse and diagonalization of a matrix
LO7.1 Compute the cofactors and the determinant of a matrix; analyze determinants in relation with row/column operations.
LO7.2 Check if a matrix is invertible; find the adjugate and the inverse of a matrix; use properties of inverses and determinants in solving problems.
LO7.3 Solve a system of linear equations using inverse matrices or Cramer's rule.
LO7.4 Find the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors to diagonalize a matrix; check if a matrix is diagonalizable.

Manipulate vector operations and linear transformations in R^3.
LO8.1 Manipulate vector operations; find equations of lines. 
LO8.2 Compute the dot product and the angle between two vectors; find the projection of a vector on another vector and manipulate equations of planes.
LO8.3 Compute the cross product; analyze areas and volumns in relation with dot and cross products.
LO8.4 Determine linear transformations in R^3 and discuss applications in computer graphic.

Find the dimension and bases of a subspace
LO9.1 Determine if a subset of vectors is a subspace; describe the subspace spanned by a set of vectors.
LO9.2 Check if a set of vectors are independent; determine if a set of vectors form a basis.
LO9.3 Find a basis and the dimension of a subspace; analyze the rank in relation with the dimension of the column, row and the null space of a matrix.
LO9.4 Compute dot product and length of vectors; check if a set of vectors are orthogonal or orthonormal; write a vector as a linear combination of an orthogonal basis.

Analytic Geometry

Matrix Decomposition

Compute the determinant of a square matrix, decide when a square matrix is invertible by equivalent conditions.
Find the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix.
Understand some theorems concerning eigenvalues.
LO1.2
Diagonalize a matrix by eigendecomposition.
Decompose a matrix by singular value decomposition.
LO1.3
Compute matrix approximation.

Vector Calculus
LO 2.1
Revisit differentiation of a univariate function.
Find Taylor expansion of a smooth function at a given point.
LO 2.2 Find partial derivatives using basic formulas and the chain rule, gradients of multivariate functions.
LO 2.3 Find gradients, Jacobian matrices of Vector-Valued Functions.
LO 2.4 Take gradients of matrices with respect to vectors.
LO 2.5 Understand the idea of backpropagation in deep learning.
LO 2.6 Find the higher-order partial derivatives, linearization and multivariate Taylor series of multivariate functions.

Probability and Distributions
LO 3.1 Catch the notions of discrete variable continuous variable; find the probability mass function, the probability density function, the cumulative distribution function and their properties.
LO 3.2 Calculate conditional probabilities; use multiplication rule, total probability rule and Bayes theorem to find probabilities.
LO 3.3 Compute the mean and variance of a random variable, compute the covariance and the correlation between two variables.
LO 3.4 Consider whether two variables are independent.
LO 3.5 Describe a Gauss distribution, marginals, conditionals, sums and products of Gauss distributions.

Continuous Optimization 
LO 4.1 Find a local minimum of a function using gradient descent.
LO 4.2 Use Lagrange multipliers to find the maximum/minimum value of a multivariate function with constraints.
LO 4.3 Understand convex optimization problems and solve linear programings.

Linear Regression 
LO 5.1 Use maximum likelihood and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation to find optimal model parameters.
LO 5.2 Using these parameter estimates to have a brief look at generalization errors and overfitting.
LO 5.3 Discuss Bayesian linear regression.

Dimensionality Reduction with PCA 
LO 6.1 Compute the data covariance matrix of a data set, construct m-dimensional subspace with maximum variance.
LO 6.2 Find the basis of theprincipal subspace.
LO 6.3 Using Low-Rank Matrix to approximate PCA.
LO 6.4 Discuss PCA in high dimension and key steps of PCA.

Classification with SVM 
LO 7.1 Understand binary classification by seperating hyperplane.
LO 7.2 Catch mathematical ideas of support vector machine.
LO 7.3 Understand the advantage of dual support vector machine.
LO 7.4 Introduce non-linear classifiers by kernels.
LO 7.5 Consider two different approaches for finding the optimal solution for the SVM.

Attitude and soft skills 
LO 8 Develop working in group skills and self-discipline

clos.details:
Discuss the DCOVA framework.
CLO1.1. Defining variables: categorical and numerical types, discrete and continuous variables, identify the measurement scales.
CLO1.2. Collecting data: population and sample, statistic and parameter, sampling methods, types of survey errors, data cleaning.
CLO1.3. Organizing variables by using Summary table, Contingency table, Ordered array, Frequency distribution, Multidimensional tables.
CLO1.4. Visualizing variables by using Charts, pitfalls in visualizing variables.
CLO1.5. Analysing data: describe the properties of Central tendency, variation and shape of distribution, boxplot, covariance and coefficient of correlation.

Discuss the basic probability rules.
CLO2.1. Understand basic probability concepts: Events, Sample spaces, Simple probability, Joint probability, Marginal probability, General addition rule.
CLO2.2. Understand Conditional probability, Multiplication rule and Determine if two events are independent.
CLO2.3. Use Bayes' theorem to revise probabilities and apply counting rules.

Describe the distribution of a variable.
CLO3.1. Discrete probability distributions, Expected value, Variance and Standard deviation of a discrete variable, Binomial and Poisson distribution, Covariance
 of a probability distribution and its application in Finance. 
CLO3.2. Compute the probabilities from the normal/uniform distribution and use the normal distribution to solve business problems.
CLO3.3. Use the normal probability plot to determine whether a set of data is approximately normally distributed.

Discuss the sampling distributions and Central limit theorem.
CLO4.1. Learn about the concept of the sampling distribution.
CLO4.2. Describe Sampling distribution of the mean and the Central limit theorem.
CLO4.3. Describe sampling distribution of the propotion.

Construct and interpret confidence interval estimates for a population parameter/ difference of population parameters. 
CLO5.1. Construct a confidence interval for the population mean/difference of two population means and interpret its meaning; determine the size of the sample 
 to improve the estimation.
CLO5.2. Construct a confidence interval for the population proportion/difference of two population pproportions and interpret its meaning; determine the size of 
 the sample to improve the estimation.

Verify a claim about a population parameter/ differnce of population parameters by using hypothesis testing. 
CLO6.1. Formulate the two hypotheses; identify critical values, test statistic and compute P-value for a test of hypotheses on population mean/difference of two 
 population means.
CLO6.2. Formulate the two hypotheses; identify critical values, test statistic and compute P-value for a test of hypotheses on population proportion/difference of 
 two population proportions.
CLO6.3. Identify type of errors in testing hypotheses.
CLO6.4. F-test for the ratio of two variances.

ANOVA analysis.
CLO7.1. Use the one-way ANOVA to test for differences among the means of several groups.
CLO7.2. Use the two-way ANOVA and interpret the interaction effect.

Regression Analysis.
CLO8.1. Discuss about Simple linear/Multiple regression models, determine the simple linear regression equation, understand the meaning of the regression 
 coefficients.
CLO8.2. Compute various sums of squares for a set of data pairs, coefficient of determination, standard error of estimate, use residual analysis to visually 
 evaluate the assumptions of regression.
CLO8.3. Determine the existence of a significant linear relationship by testing for the Slope and Correlation coefficient.
CLO8.4. Evaluate the overall multiple regression model: the coefficient of multiple determination, the adjusted r square, the overall F test.

Be able to present a decision making for a business problem.
CLO9.1. Be able to work in a team or individually in making business decisions based on Statistical analysis/ Statistical package (Excel).
CLO9.2. Understand of being ethical when conducting statistical analysis.

clos.details:
Discuss the roles of statistics in engineering
LO1.1 Explain the types of reasoning of statistical inference; distinguish mechanistic models and empirical models, statistic and parameter, sample and population.
LO1.2 Describe the different methods that engineers use to collect data.

Identify sample spaces and events, and use basic rules to calculate the probability of an event
LO2.1 Describe the sample space and events of an experiment; distinguish continuous and discrete sample spaces; perform operations on events.
LO2.2 Calculate the probability of an event in a discrete sample space; use addition and complementary rules to find probabilities.
LO2.3 Calculate conditional probabilities; use multiplication rule, total probability rule and Bayes theorem to find probabilities. 
LO2.4 Determine if two events are independent; use independence to find probabilities.
LO2.5 Recognize a random variable; distinguish continuous and discrete random variables.

Describe the probability distribution and calculate the mean and variance of a discrete random variable
LO3.1 Describe a discrete random variable; check if a function is a probability mass function and use it to calculate probability; find the cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable.
LO3.2 Compute the mean and variance of a discrete random variable. 
LO3.3 Determine the probability, mean and variance of uniform, binomial, geometric and negative binomial, hypergeometric and Poisson distributions.

Describe the probability distribution and calculate the mean and variance of a continuous random variable
LO4.1 Describe a continuous random variable; check if a function is a probability density function and use it to calculate probability; find the cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable.
LO4.2 Compute the mean and variance of a continuous random variables
LO4.3 Apply the formulas of continuous uniform distribution and exponential distribution to solve problems.
LO4.4 Manipulate probabilities of a standard normal distribution using Excel or table of data; standardize a normal distribution.
LO4.5 Use normal distribution to approximate binomial and Poisson distributions.

Describe data using numerical summaries and visual displays
LO5.1 Find numeric summaries of data; describe data using stem-and-leaf diagrams, frequency distributions, histograms, time series plots. 
LO5.2 Determine quartiles and construct the box plot for a data; identify outliers.

Discuss sampling distributions and use the Central Limit Theorem to analyze sampling distribution of the means
LO6.1 Discuss sampling distributions; find the point estimation of a parameter.
LO6.2 Apply Central Limit Theorem to calculate probabilities regarding the sampling distribution of the means.

Construct confidence intervals for a population parameter/difference of population parameters
LO7.1 Construct a confidence interval for the population mean/difference of two population means and interpret its meaning; determine the size of the sample to improve the estimation.
LO7.2 Construct a confidence interval for the population proportion/difference of two population pproportions and interpret its meaning; determine the size of the sample to improve the estimation.

Verify a claim about a population parameter/difference of population parameters using hypothesis testing
LO8.1 Formulate the two hypotheses; identify critical values, test statistic and compute P-value for a test of hypotheses on population mean/difference of two population means
LO8.2 Formulate the two hypotheses; identify critical values, test statistic and compute P-value for a test of hypotheses on population proportion/difference of two population proportions
LO8.3 Identify type of errors in testing hypotheses.

Construct a simple linear regression model
LO9.1 Compute various sums of squares for a set of data pairs.
LO9.2 Determine the equation of linear regression and the correlation coefficient; use linear regression to predict future values.
LO9.3 Perform a hypothesis test in simple linear regression; test the significance of regression using t-test.

MCE201.description: This course provides students with a fundamental understanding of measurement and control engineering. Through practical exercises and simulations, students will develop the skills to perform measurements, collect and interpret data, and evaluate the behavior of measurement and control systems.

assessments.note:
Option 1: 
Task Description:
Find your culture (subculture) and embrace your own culture. This assessment provides you with an opportunity to reflect on your culture as an "insider". You are required to apply at least one of the theories or conceptual models you have learned in the course. This assessment provides you with an opportunity to identify who you are, which culture you belong to and the characteristics of your culture group.
Presentation:
For the 6-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your essay in front of your classmates to help them gain insights into your culture and acknowledge how they should communicate with you with the purpose of mutual collaboration and harmony. It help you become aware of the fact that how your cultural identity affects your communications.
Essay:
Your reflective essay conveys who you are as a member of a cultural group, what beliefs, values, practices, traditions and so forth are considered as important in your culture, and why they are important for members of your culture. Reflecting on your own culture will greatly help you to understand you and other cultures (which is the purpose of Assessment 2). Your cultural group can be defined at national level (e.g.,Vietnamese) or at sub-cultural level (e.g., ethnic groups, hobby groups). An example of a theoretical model that you may choose to use in your assignment is Dodd's model of culture. You may apply it to explain how the values within the inner core of a culture are reflected in the attitudes and behaviours of your cultural group. You need to define all key concepts used in the theories or theoretical models you have chosen to include in your essay so that you can demonstrate your understanding of knowledge and your ability to apply it.
Include the following sections in your reflective essay:
• Title of your essay.
• Brief description of the cultural group with which you identify, including values, beliefs, traditions, or customs that you choose to focus on.
• Definition and explanation of the theories and/or the conceptual model you choose to frame the discussion of your culture.
• Your reflection on what it means to you to identify as a member of your cultural group, and how your cultural identity shapes your thinking and doing. 
Notes: The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer. 4

Task Description:
The assessment, including one group report and one group presentation, provides you with an opportunity to understand your future target audience by experiencing their culture/subculture as an "outsider".
As communicators, we want our audience to receive our messages and understand them as we intended them regardless of different culture identity. This project can help you to come up with some ideas to tailor your messages, visual content and pick the media channels you may use to reach your target audiences. Students will work in group of 2 or 3 in order to conduct this project. 
Presentation:
For the 30-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates to help them gain insights into various cultures/subcultures, and all challenges they may have to face in the future regrading cross cultural conflict and misunderstanding. Your presentation should showcase how we can communicate with our target audiences to spread the right message using the right media platforms.
Report:
To accomplish this assignment, you need to:
• Conduct some serious research into a culture/subculture and the people who have belonged to this culture group
• Attend and participate (at least) one cultural event. This event should be organised by members of a culture (or subculture) other than your own. Examples of these cultural events include, but not limited to, cultural fairs, weddings, celebration of festivals, etc. You may need to search the internet, and any other sources in order to locate those cultural events.
• Formulate at least 10 questions you want to ask people from that culture about their experiences of being a member of that cultural group.
• Interview 3-5 people from this cultural group at the event. You may also observe their interactions and behaviours at the event.
• Identify a problem or a set of related problems leading to miscommunication between members of this cultural group and you (e.g., stereotypes, different value orientations, communication styles, etc.).
• Apply at least one theory (or one conceptual model) to analyse the identified intercultural problem (e.g., value orientations, high-context and low-context culture, communication accommodation, etc.).
• Reflect on your learning through this intercultural experience, suggest some methods to approach your target audiences who belong to the culture and recommend some types of appropriate content which can resonate with them and some media platforms which can reach them.
Include the following sections in your report:
• Title of the report.
• Introduction: State the culture you have chosen and provide a justification for your choice of the cultural group and the event to attend.
• The event: Provide a brief description of the event and its significance to the people who organised it.
• Observations and interactions: Explain what you observed at the event that you understood accurately and what was puzzling to you. Describe your interview questions and your interviewees (e.g., why do you choose to interview them; what are the major findings from the interviews).
• Problems, solutions, suggestions and application of theories: Identify what people think might be the major difficulties in communication between people from diffrent cultural groups. Analyse the potential problems by drawing on theories and concepts learned in the course. Provide some suggestions in order to approach the target audiences effectively and positively.
• Reflection: Reflect on your experience of interacting with people in a different cultural situation that is not as predictable as communicating in your familiar cultural environment; and discuss what you have learned from this intercultural experience
Notes: The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.
Each group will need to conduct an in-depth interview (choice of person interviewed to be approved by the instructor) and include the full transcript of the interview in the annex section of the report. It is expected that between 10 and 12 questions be raised during the interview.

MCO302.description: This course introduces students to the foundational theories and pressing issues in intercultural communication, with a particular focus on how culture and identity shape human interaction. Through a thematic approach and the use of authentic materials, students engage with real-world examples of communication across cultural boundaries—learning not only how meaning is constructed, but also how it can be misunderstood or transformed in diverse contexts.As the course progresses, students build a solid understanding of how cultural frameworks influence perception, behavior, and dialogue. They develop the ability to communicate effectively and ethically across cultures, learning to navigate both verbal and nonverbal cues with sensitivity. Special emphasis is placed on the responsible use of digital tools and AI technologies to support communication and solve problems in multicultural environments.Beyond knowledge and skills, the course fosters a mindset of openness and respect. Students are encouraged to reflect critically on their own cultural assumptions, embrace diversity, and approach global interactions with empathy and integrity. By the end of the course, they are not only better communicators, but also more thoughtful participants in an increasingly interconnected world.

clos.details: Understand the fundamentals of an embedded system and discover the ARM architecture and microcontrollers.
Understand the characteristics of microcontrollers and embedded systems, including their components, benefits, and constraints.
Understand the industry-standard ARM-based microcontroller architecture, its features, and programming models.
Develop working embedded prototypes using the STM32 HAL library, FreeRTOS, the ST Nucleo-F401RE board (or ST Nucleo-F411RE board), and low-cost peripherals.
Apply knowledge of digital and analog I/O programming on STM32 microcontrollers.
Implement interrupts to control peripherals using the STM32 HAL library.
Develop applications incorporating timers and Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) using the STM32 HAL library.
Evaluate serial communication protocols used in embedded systems (UART, SPI, and I2C), including their benefits and limitations.

MCP201.description: Hands-on Embedded Systems Development: Learn to implement real-world embedded system projects on microcontrollers (using both simulation environments and physical hardware) with the STM32Cube HAL library and STM32CubeIDE.Peripheral Mastery & ARM Architecture: Master the core architecture of the ARM Cortex-M processor. Develop and refine C/C++ source code to build diverse applications (signal generators, temperature monitoring systems, audio players, and user interfaces) by leveraging Digital/Analog I/O, Interrupts, Timers, and Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM). Gain hands-on proficiency in analyzing and deploying serial communication protocols—SPI, UART, and I2C—while evaluating their advantages and limitations in embedded environments.Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS): Explore the core characteristics of RTOS and multitasking mechanisms on microcontrollers. Students will directly apply Threads, Mutexes, Semaphores, and Interrupts to design a complete multitasking system, effectively resolving resource contention issues.Practical Engineering Skills: Prototype embedded systems using the ST Nucleo-F401RE (ST Nucleo-F411RE) development board and cost-effective components. Enhance hardware-level C/C++ programming mindsets by immediately applying theory to practice. Master the end-to-end hardware development workflow alongside professional debugging and troubleshooting techniques.

MED201.description:
Description: This course will give you a thorough explanation of how media technologies develop, operate, converge, and affect society in order to think critically about the media and its effects on culture. It provides a comprehensive introduction to today's global media environment and the ongoing developments in technology, culture, and critical theory that continue to transform this rapidly evolving industry and affect your everyday life. Our emphasis is on the social relations of power and connectivity that are shaped by new media as practices of communication. Specific topics that will be explored include: the latest developments and trends in social media, e-publishing, policy changes for Internet governance, online privacy protection, online ad exchanges, the changing video game industry, and much more. By studying this course, students will develop knowledge and skills in creative thinking, communication, collaboration, planning, critical analysis, and digital and ethical citizenship.
Teaching methods: Direct Instruction, Inquiry-based Learning, Cooperative Learning, Case Study Analysis

clos.details: Identify and characterize multimodal AI systems and the four core problems of multimodal machine learning - representation, alignment, fusion, and translation.
Build cross-modal representations using contrastive and self-supervised methods, and evaluate them via zero-shot transfer and cross-modal retrieval.
Design and implement fusion architectures (cross-attention, latent bottlenecks, connector modules) that combine heterogeneous modalities.
Apply vision-language and unified multimodal architectures (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, and unified token/diffusion-transformer families) and instruction-tune them.
Apply multimodal techniques to non-image modalities - speech, audio, video, 3D, and embodied agents - and to cross-modal generation.
Engineer multimodal reasoning, agent, and retrieval systems, and address the input-size and latency challenges of deploying them.
Evaluate multimodal systems with appropriate benchmarks and protocols, recognizing saturation and the migrating frontier, and run hallucination and grounding diagnostics.
Analyze the safety, provenance, bias, and privacy issues specific to multimodal AI - deepfakes, watermarking, and biometric data.

MGA301.description: Multimodal AI course aim on building AI systems that operate across modalities - vision, language, audio, video, 3D, and embodiment. The course frames multimodality through four core problems (representation, alignment, fusion, translation) and proceeds through cross-modal representations (CLIP, SigLIP, ImageBind), fusion architectures (cross-attention, Perceiver, Q-Former, gated cross-attention), vision-language and unified models (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, Chameleon/Janus families), speech and audio, video and world models, 3D and embodied agents, multimodal reasoning / agents / RAG, evaluation (benchmark saturation, hallucination), efficiency and deployment, and safety/provenance/frontiers. Mathematical depth is assumed from the prerequisites (Deep Learning, Advanced Generative AI); this course focuses on architectures, training recipes, evaluation, and hands-on multimodal systems.

MGT102.description:
Khóa học tập trung xung quanh các vấn đề quản trị　cơ bản. Khóa học được thiết kế để cung cấp các kiến thức cơ bản về chuyên ngành đồng thời giới thiệu và phân tích các ví dụ thực tiễn giúp học sinh dễ nắm bắt kiến thức cũng như sẽ có khả năng áp dụng các kiến thức đã học được một cách linh hoạt vào việc xem xét môi trường quản trị thực tế. 
Sinh viên có nhiệm vụ đọc và tìm hiểu chuẩn bị kiến thức trước khi lên lớp, tham gia tích cực vào những phần trao đổi thảo luận trên lớp, đồng thời có trách nhiêm hoàn thành bài thuyết trình cá nhân cũng như bài tập nhóm. Các hoạt động này sẽ giúp sinh viên chủ động trong việc tìm hiểu và tiếp thu kiến thức, phát huy tinh thần tích cực trong hoat động nhóm. Hơn thế, vốn tiếng Nhật (cả về lượng từ vựng lẫn các kỹ năng viết và nói) sẽ tăng lên theo các hoạt động đa dạng mà khóa học đề ra.

clos.details: Understand the fundamentals of an embedded system and discover the ARM architecture and microcontrollers.
Understand the characteristics of microcontrollers and embedded systems, including their components, benefits, and constraints.
Understand the industry-standard ARM-based microcontroller architecture, its features, and programming models.
Develop working embedded prototypes using the STM32 HAL library, FreeRTOS, the ST Nucleo-F401RE board (or ST Nucleo-F411RE board), and low-cost peripherals.
Apply knowledge of digital and analog I/O programming on STM32 microcontrollers.
Implement interrupts to control peripherals using the STM32 HAL library.
Develop applications incorporating timers and Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) using the STM32 HAL library.
Evaluate serial communication protocols used in embedded systems (UART, SPI, and I2C), including their benefits and limitations.
Understand Real-Time Operating Systems (FreeRTOS) and how they facilitate multitasking in embedded systems.
Implement real-world embedded system projects on the STM32 Nucleo board using FreeRTOS, with proper task synchronization (Mutex/Semaphore).

MIP201.description: Hands-on Embedded Systems Development: Learn to implement real-world embedded system projects on microcontrollers (using both simulation environments and physical hardware) with the STM32Cube HAL library and STM32CubeIDE.Peripheral Mastery & ARM Architecture: Master the core architecture of the ARM Cortex-M processor. Develop and refine C/C++ source code to build diverse applications (signal generators, temperature monitoring systems, audio players, and user interfaces) by leveraging Digital/Analog I/O, Interrupts, Timers, and Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM). Gain hands-on proficiency in analyzing and deploying serial communication protocols—SPI, UART, and I2C—while evaluating their advantages and limitations in embedded environments.Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS): Explore the core characteristics of RTOS and multitasking mechanisms on microcontrollers. Students will directly apply Threads, Mutexes, Semaphores, and Interrupts to design a complete multitasking system, effectively resolving resource contention issues.Practical Engineering Skills: Prototype embedded systems using the ST Nucleo-F401RE (ST Nucleo-F411RE) development board and cost-effective components. Enhance hardware-level C/C++ programming mindsets by immediately applying theory to practice. Master the end-to-end hardware development workflow alongside professional debugging and troubleshooting techniques.

clos.details: Explain key concepts, frameworks, and principles of content marketing, including audience analysis, buyer journey mapping, brand voice, and content strategy development.
Apply strategic frameworks (e.g., SMART goals, content calendars, and storytelling models such as CREATE) to design and implement coherent, multi-channel content marketing plans.
Analyze audience insights, content performance metrics, and KPIs to evaluate the effectiveness of content marketing campaigns and recommend data-driven improvements.
Create persuasive and engaging content (e.g., headlines, copywriting, storytelling formats) tailored to different platforms and target audiences to achieve specific marketing objectives.

Utilize AI tools and technologies in the content marketing process to enhance ideation, content production, personalization, and optimization while critically assessing their effectiveness and ethical implications.

Develop and present a comprehensive, project-based content marketing strategy that integrates course knowledge (strategy, execution, distribution, and measurement) to address a real or simulated business problem.

MKC201m.description: This Course is based on the Coursera Specialization "Content Marketing," which covers both the theorical and practical lessons of content marketing. Specifically, students will be equipped with the strategic frameworks, tools, and decision-making skills needed to plan, create, optimize, and scale content in today’s digital landscape. Students will progress from foundational content strategy and audience engagement to advanced tactics for optimization, production scaling, and performance measurement.Additionally, students will explore how to align content with business goals, design content systems using pillars and topic clusters, apply modern SEO and discoverability best practices, and responsibly scale production using AI, partnerships, and repurposing strategies. Throughout the specialization, students focus on building content that is not only engaging, but discoverable, credible, and sustainable over time. They will apply the acquired knowledge and skills in completing a project to tackle a specified real-world problem.

MKG101.description:
The course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of both classical and contemporary marketing theories, as well as their practical applications. Throughout the course, students will engage with new classical and contemporary cases, exploring the interdisciplinary and cross-functional implications of business management theories, contemporary marketing management principles, and futuristic applications of marketing management theories and concepts. Upon successful completion of this course, students shall:
1. Acquire an understanding of the significance of management and marketing in various organisational settings.
2. Gain a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles that govern management and marketing.
3. Demonstrate outstanding analytic abilities that are critical for effectively tackling obstacles in business and marketing operations and reaching well-informed managerial judgements.

MKT101.description:
The course is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in marketing based on five key activities: (1) identifying customer needs, (2) providing customers with the right products or service to meet their needs, (3) assuring availability to customers through the right distribution channels, (4) using promotional activities in ways that motivate purchase as effectively as possible, (5) setting an appropriate price that maximizes firm profitability while maintaining customer satisfaction.
The Principle of Marketing course (Philip Kotler) integrates AI tools as supportive instruments for idea generation, document organization, and the practical application of marketing concepts. Students will employ AI for brainstorming, content structuring, creation of marketing materials, and basic analytics, while retaining full responsibility for ensuring originality, critical evaluation, and refinement of their work. The course also equips students to assess the strengths and limitations of AI-generated outputs and to identify ethical risks such as plagiarism and bias.
Tools Utilized:
- lmarena AI: For generating marketing-related data and insights.
- Statista: For accessing statistical data and market research.
- ChatGPT: For idea generation, structuring documents, and simulating real-life marketing scenarios.
- Canva: For creating visual marketing materials like infographics, templates, and videos.
The assessment methods have been reformed to more accurately reflect students’ actual competencies. Learners are evaluated through oral examinations, presentations, group debates, and the assessment of submitted products, as well as through their selection of prompts, which demonstrate their thinking process, revisions, and interactions with AI feedback.

MKT201.description: Main objectives:This course is designed to provide students with essential and working knowledge of the terminology and concepts in the field of consumer behavior and a better understanding of how consumers make choices and how their choices ultimately affect their well-being. After taking this class, the students should all be able to: (1) Understand basic concepts and major research that has relevance to consumer behaviour(2) Integrate these concepts into a framework that can be applied to the analysis of the individual consumer and the market(3) Analyse and understand consumer's decision making process(4) Apply consumer behaviour in the development and implementation of marketing tactics and strategies.Description: This course will review concepts, issues, and methods applicable to the study of consumer behavior. It is divided into 4 main parts: (1) Psychological characteristics of consumers; (2) Social and external factors influencing consumer behavior; (3) The role of sub-culture and culture; and (4) Consumer decision-making process. Class discussions, case study analysis , practical activities, along with group projects and quizzes will provide the basis for the learning environment in the classroom.The assignment requires students to integrate AI throughout the project, leveraging it for ideation, structuring, content generation, and analysis. The primary level of using AI is "AI Task Completion, Human Evaluation", with creative aspects edging into the "Full AI", as students rely on AI to achieve creative outputs collaboratively while critically engaging with its results.

clos.details: Use the product/market growth matrix to explain the various ways a company can expand globally and Briefly explain how exchange rates impact a company’s opportunities in different parts of the world.

Describe the available alternatives for conflict resolution and dispute settlement when doing business outside the home country and compare and contrast single-country marketing strategy with global marketing strategy (GMS).
Compare and contrast the four main categories of preferential trade agreements in Latin America and Asia
Define culture and identify the various expressions and manifestations of culture that can impact global marketing strategies.
Explain the concept of environmental sensitivity and give contrasting examples of product categories that are deeply embedded in culture and those that are not.
Understand the elements of a country’s political environment that can impact global marketing activities.
Define international law and describe the main types of legal systems found in different parts of the world.
Discuss the role of information technology in a global company’s decision-making processes.
Identify the variables that global marketers can use to segmentation, targeting, and positioning global markets and give an example of each.
Describe the various positioning options available to global marketers and Understand the difference between export selling and export marketing.
Describe the various national policies that pertain to exports and imports and Explain the structure of the harmonized tariff system.
Describe the various organizations that support and facilitate the export process and Compare between home-country and market-country export organization considerations.
Discuss the factors that contribute to the successful launch of a global strategic partnership.

Compare and contrast local products and brands, international products and brands, and global products and brands and the five strategic alternatives that marketers can utilize during the global product planning process.
Identify the different pricing strategies and objectives that influence decisions about pricing products in global markets and some of the environmental influences that impact prices.
Identify and compare the basic structure options for consumer channels and industrial channels and Describe the different categories of retail operations that are found in various parts of the world.

Define sales promotion and identify the most important promotion tactics and tools used by global marketers and Compare between publicity and public relations and identify global companies that have recently been impacted by negative publicity.
Analyze the major innovations and trends that underline the digital revolution and Describe the different organizational structures that companies can adopt and they grow and expand globally.
Define hypercompetitive industry and list the key arenas in which dynamic strategic interactions take place.

MKT204.description:
This course examines the opportunities and challenges associated with global marketing. The impact on marketing of the cultural, economic, political, and technological environments in different countries will be discussed. The relationship between global marketing and global business strategy will be reviewed. Strategies and tactics for developing each of the four "P's" internationally and globally will be examined, including developing:
• Product, service, and branding policies, 
• Advertising, promotion, and communications plans, 
• Channels of distributions 
• Pricing policies in the global context. 
Approaches for deciding the extent to which marketing should be globalized versus localized will be explored. This course will examine key considerations in marketing both globally and in each of the major regions of the world.

clos.details: Understand the basic foundations of international marketing and be able to explain how companies can grow by going abroad or sourcing ideas/expanding into other countries or industries.
Understand the core meaning of marketing and international marketing.

Learn that international marketing is about striking the right balance between maximizing the similarities across cultures (Etic approach) and customizing marketing (Emic approach) to important local differences.
Learn about how to source or expand into other industries at home or abroad via cross industry innovation.
Obtain a solid foundation for subsequent courses in the specialization.

Understand consumer science investigation, B2C marketing, International Marketing Entry, Targeting, Positioning, International Product, International Promotion, International Place and International Price
Learn how to approach consumers as science investigators from a business to consumer standpoint (B2C).
Understand how to enter international markets, select targets and position their brands.

Achieve deeper insights into the core meaning of international marketing elements, i.e. product, promotion, place, and price in the international marketing context, and their inter-element relationships with each other.
Acquire new thinking about innovating in marketing with the 7S approach: social, small, simple, skip, sports, screen, and set marketing with cross-country and cross-industry innovation implications.
Understand the differentiating aspects of business to business (B2B) marketing that can be contrasted to traditional business to consumer (B2C) marketing
Understand the differences between B2C and B2B marketing.
Approach marketing problems from an inter-organizational perspective, in particular, learn about decision making at buying centers.
Innovate B2B marketing via a CCCI, i.e. Cross Country & Cross Industry Innovation approach.
Gain insights about CCCI Innovation and best practices via interviews with top B2B industry experts.
Understand the unique characteristics of both hospitality and healthcare services sector.

Identify the unique characteristics of service businesses and create successful management strategies to better manage the role of customers to gain desirable business outcomes, better market products than are intangible, and better manage customer expectations and perceptions.

Identify the unique characteristics of the hospitality industry, explain the process of balancing supply and demand in the hospitality industry, and implement optimal marketing and management strategies for this unique market.

Identify the unique characteristics of the healthcare industry, explain how this industry is evolving into the experience business, and better manage human interactions and facility to enhance the quality of customer experience.
Gain insights from the innovative approaches in the service industry overall, in hospitality and health industry in particular, and better develop innovative strategies in your industry.
Understand the characteristics and marketing strategies related to two key global industries, sports and entertainment.
Learn the key characteristics of sports marketing.
Learn the key characteristics of entertainment marketing.
Be able to apply cross country growth strategies to your business in the sports and entertainment industry.
Be able to apply cross industry growth strategies to your business in the sports and entertainment industry”.
Be able to reference CCCI, i.e. cross-country and cross-industry Innovation best practices via interviews with key experts in the sports and entertainment industry.
Be able to apply what you have learned during the 16 weeks of the 5 courses
Be able to perform Situation Analysis for your chosen company or brand.
Be able to perform Marketing Mix Analysis for your chosen company or brand.
Be able to construct Cross Country Innovation Plan when expanding abroad.
Be able to construct Cross Industry Innovation Plan when sourcing ideas or expanding into another industry.

MKT205.description: This Specialization covers marketing concepts but, more importantly, emphasizes the need by companies and individuals to think openly across international markets and industries for new ideas or expansion. This is summarized as "Cross Country & Cross Industry" Innovation, or CCCI in short. The first two courses will establish the core foundations and then the last three courses will elaborate on major global industry clusters: course 3 on B2B, course 4 on Healthcare and Hospitality, and course 5 on Sports and Entertainment. The capstone will require learners to develop a new product using knowledge learned from at least 2 industries.

MKT209m.description:
This Course is based on the both Coursera Specialization "The Strategy of Content Marketing" and "Social Media Management", which covers both the theorical and practical lessons of content marketing. You firstly will learn the core strategies content marketers use to acquire and retain customers profitably. Specifically, you will learn how to develop, organize and implement a content marketing strategy, analyze and measure the effectiveness of content marketing, write compelling copy, use a strategic framework when writing, and build your professional brand and authority through content marketing. You will also learn how to put the ideas presented to you into action and build your own personal brand through content marketing. You will end the course with real-world application of your skills through a content management project on social media. 
This is a blended-learning course, in which students will take a look at the videos & slides and reading on Coursera first at home, then rewatch & discuss key questions with classmates and teachers at classes.
AI tools can significantly enhance content marketing efforts by automating tasks, improving content quality, and providing valuable insights. Some AI tools that can be used in content marketing include: 
AI Writing Tools, AI Design Tools, AI Social Media Management Tools, AI Analytics Tools

clos.details:
Cung cấp những hiểu biết có tính căn bản, hệ thống về triết học Marx - Lenin. Nắm vững những nét khái quát nhất về triết học, triết học Mác – Lênin và vai trò của triết học Mác – Lênin trong đời sống xã hội
To provide fundamental and systematic knowledge of Marxist–Leninist philosophy. To grasp the most general features of philosophy, Marxist–Leninist philosophy, and the role of Marxist–Leninist philosophy in social life.

Nắm vững nội dung của chủ nghĩa duy vật biện chứng: vấn đề vật chất và ý thức; phép biện chứng duy vật; lý luận nhận thức của chủ nghĩa duy vật biện chứng
Master knowledge of dialectical materialism: matter and consciousness; materialistic dialectics; cognition theory of dialectical materialism

Đánh giá được các nội dung của chủ nghĩa duy vật lịch sử: vấn đề hình thái kinh tế - xã hội; giai cấp và dân tộc; nhà nước và cách mạng xã hội chủ nghĩa; ý thức xã hội; triết học về con người
Be able to evaluate matters of historical materialism: the theory of socio-economic forms, class and peoples; state and revolution; social consciousness; philosophical theory of humans

Hình thành tư duy triết học trong quá trình nhận thức và đánh giá được một số vấn đề lý luận và thực tiễn. Nhận thức được thực chất giá trị, bản chất khoa học và cách mạng của triết học Marx - Lenin
To develop philosophical thinking in the process of cognition and to be able to evaluate certain theoretical and practical issues. To understand the true value, scientific nature, and revolutionary essence of Marxist–Leninist philosophy.

Vận dụng được các quy luật của triết học Mác – Lênin vào phân tích, nhận định, đánh giá và giải quyết các vấn đề kinh tế - xã hội
Apply the laws of Marxism – Leninism philosophy to analyze, identify, evaluate and solve socio-economic problems

Xây dựng thế giới quan duy vật biện chứng và phương pháp luận biện chứng duy vật làm nền tảng lý luận cho việc nhận thức vấn đề, nội dung của các môn học khác. Hình thành các phương pháp luận chung nhất làm cơ sở nhận thức cho các chuyên ngành đào tạo. Hình thành thế giới quan, phương pháp luận thích ứng trước sự biến đổi nhanh chóng của thời đại, khoa học công nghệ.
To develop a materialist worldview and dialectical materialist methodology as a theoretical foundation for understanding issues and the content of other subjects. To establish the most general methodological foundations as a basis for knowledge in specialized disciplines. To foster a worldview and methodology capable of adapting to the rapid transformations of the era and advances in science and technology.

Củng cố niềm tin của người học vào cuộc sống, các chủ trương, đường lối của Đảng, chính sách và pháp luật của Nhà nước. Hình thành năng lực lý luận và ứng dụng thực tiễn, nhấn mạnh vai trò công dân và tinh thần trách nhiệm xã hội.
Consolidate students' confidence in life, in guidelines and policies of the Party, and in policies and laws of the States. To develop reasoning competence and practical application skills, with an emphasis on civic roles and social responsibility.

Xây dựng kỹ năng lập luận, soạn thảo bài viết, thuyết trình, ứng dụng AI, sáng tạo trong việc thực hiện sản phẩm, tư duy phản biện, xử lý các quan hệ xã hội và hoạt động nhóm. Xây dựng kỹ năng thích ứng, tự học, sử dụng AI có trách nhiệm, đạo đức phù hợp với quan điểm triết học Mác - Lênin, văn hóa - xã hội, lịch sử Việt Nam
To develop skills in reasoning, academic writing, presentation, AI application, creativity in product implementation, critical thinking, social relations management, and teamwork. To build adaptability and self-learning skills, and to use AI responsibly and ethically in alignment with Marx - Lenin philosophical perspectives as well as Vietnam’s cultural, social, and historical context.

MLN111.description:
Giới thiệu môn học: Triết học Mác - Lênin nghiên cứu những quan điểm duy vật biện chứng về tự nhiên, xã hội, tư duy và nhờ đó thế giới quan duy vật biện chứng trở thành toàn diện và triệt để. Áp dụng và mở rộng quan điểm duy vật biện chứng vào nghiên cứu xã hội, Mác đã đưa ra được quan niệm duy vật về lịch sử, chỉ ra con đường nghiên cứu những quy luật của sự phát triển xã hội, cũng như sự phát triển của tự nhiên, không phải do ý muốn chủ quan mà do những quy luật khách quan quyết định. Sự ra đời của Triết học Mác - Lênin đã đặt cơ sở cho việc nghiên cứu lịch sử và đời sống xã hội thực sự có tính chất khoa học.
Course introduction: Philosophy of Marxism – Leninism studies dialectical materialistic views on nature, society, and the mind, making the worldview of dialectical materialism becomes comprehensive. Applying and expanding the dialectical materialist perspective to social research, Marx has introduced historical materialism and pointed out the way to study the laws of social development and natural development governed by objective laws rather than subjective factors. The development of Marxism – Leninism philosophy has laid the foundation for the study of history and social life in a scientific way.

Môn học Triết học Mác-Lênin nhằm giúp cho sinh viên: Cung cấp những hiểu biết có tính căn bản, hệ thống về triết học Mác - Lênin. Xây dựng thế giới quan duy vật và phương pháp luận biện chứng duy vật làm nền tảng lí luận cho việc nhận thức các vấn đề, nội dung của các môn học khác. Nhận thức được thực chất giá trị, bản chất khoa học, cách mạng của triết học Mác - Lênin. Dịch chuyển từ "truyền thụ kiến thức một chiều" sang hình thành tư duy phản biện, năng lực lý luận và ứng dụng thực tiễn, nhấn mạnh vai trò công dân và tinh thần trách nhiệm xã hội.
“The course Marxist–Leninist Philosophy aims to help students: provide fundamental and systematic knowledge of Marxist–Leninist philosophy; develop a materialist worldview and dialectical materialist methodology as a theoretical foundation for understanding issues and the content of other subjects; recognize the true value, scientific nature, and revolutionary essence of Marxist–Leninist philosophy; and shift from ‘one-way knowledge transmission’ to the development of critical thinking, reasoning competence, and practical application, with an emphasis on civic roles and social responsibility.

Nội dung môn học bao gồm các chương: Chương 1: Trình bày những nét khái quát nhất về triết học, triết học Mác – Lênin và vai trò của triết học Mác – Lênin trong đời sống xã hội. Chương 2: Trình bày những nội dung cơ bản của chủ nghĩa duy vật biện chứng, gồm vấn đề vật chất và ý thức; phép biện chứng duy vật; lý luận nhận thức của chủ nghĩa duy vật biện chứng. Chương 3: Trình bày những nội dung cơ bản của chủ nghĩa duy vật lịch sử, gồm vấn đề hình thái kinh tế - xã hội; giai cấp và dân tộc; nhà nước và cách mạng; ý thức xã hội; triết học về con người. 
The course includes chapters: Chapter 1: Present an overview of philosophy, Marxism – Leninism philosophy, and the role of Marxist-Leninist philosophy in social life. Chapter 2: Present basic issues of dialectical materialism including matter and consciousness; materialistic dialectics; cognition theory of dialectical materialism. Chapter 3: Present basic issues of historical materialism including the theory of socio-economic forms, class and peoples; state and revolution; social consciousness; philosophical theory of humans.
